fr_passeport_noun.hook: A girl in a yellow raincoat shows her PASSPORT at the window while the rain POURS down: PASS, POUR! pahs-POR.
fr_passeport_noun.why: Duck in a raincoat replaced by a human girl (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_rendez_vous_noun.hook: A boy with a bouquet checks his pocket watch: his RENDEZVOUS is late! English borrowed the same word: rahn-day-VOO.
fr_rendez_vous_noun.why: Hedgehog replaced by a human boy (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_ficelle_noun.hook: TWINE is wound round the neck of a CELLO: fee-SEHL = fi-CELL(o)!
fr_ficelle_noun.why: Old hook described a shop-mouse that is not painted; the painted cello with twine is now the hook.

fr_stylo_noun.hook: A STYLISH PEN in a pink scarf leans on the desk, striking a pose: STY-LO! stee-LOH.
fr_stylo_noun.why: Desk zoom re-cut from the town hall painting; the pen there wears a pink scarf (its sunglasses are too small to see), so the hook names only what is visible.

fr_feuille_noun_2.hook: This SHEET of writing paper is cut in the shape of a LEAF, because French uses one word for both: une feuille (de papier).
fr_feuille_noun_2.why: RECS 1.4: paper sense split from the leaf (fr_feuille_noun, foret/arbres).

fr_ainsi_adv.hook: ANN ("an-") says "SEE ("-SEE")? You fold the ballot THUS, in this way" and shows the young man how to mail it in the box.
fr_ainsi_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_assez_adv.hook: A councillor keeps pouring water until the glass overflows, and the bald man beside her raises a hand: "I SAY ("ah-SAY"), that's ENOUGH!"
fr_assez_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_certainement_adv.hook: Like English 'certainly', said sehr-teh-nuh-MAHN: a knight councillor holds up all TEN fingers: "CERTAINLY, SIR, TEN times over!"
fr_certainement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_donc_adv.hook: The councillor brings down his gavel: DONK ("DOHNK")! SO, THEREFORE, the motion is passed.
fr_donc_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_enfin_adv.hook: After a sweltering wait, a councillor pulls the cord and the ceiling fan is finally ON: "ON FAN ("ahn-FAN"), AT LAST!"
fr_enfin_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_ensuite_adv.hook: The bearded councillor waits to speak NEXT, holding one big SWEET ("ahn-SWEET"): first the gavel, THEN it's his turn.
fr_ensuite_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_peut_etre_adv.hook: A gray-haired councillor's hand PUPPET ("peuh-TEHTR") shrugs its little shoulders: PERHAPS yes, PERHAPS no.
fr_peut_etre_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_seulement_adv.hook: A councillor proudly holds up a SALMON ("suh-luh-MAHN"): he caught ONLY one!
fr_seulement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_evidemment_adv.hook: Like English 'evidently', said ay-vee-dah-MAHN: A VIDEO MAN films the cat beside the pie, crumbs scattered round it: OF COURSE the cat nibbled the pie.
fr_evidemment_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_absolument_adv.hook: Like English 'absolutely', said ahp-soh-lew-MAHN: a red-haired councillor bangs the gallery rail and roars "ABSOLUTELY!", making every inkpot jump into the air.
fr_absolument_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_certes_adv.hook: "ADMITTEDLY, it's a CERT ("SEHRT")", smiles the gray-haired councillor, holding up her certificate with its red seal, "but let's vote anyway."
fr_certes_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_d_ailleurs_adv.hook: BESIDES the roses, the vase holds one big pink DAHLIA ("dah-YUHR").
fr_d_ailleurs_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_heureusement_adv.hook: FORTUNATELY the striped circus strongman dives and catches the falling pitcher just in time: "HURRAH'S ("uh-RUHZ") the MAN ("mon")!"
fr_heureusement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_probablement_adv.hook: Like English 'probably', said proh-bah-bluh-MAHN: a councillor at the gallery window grabs her umbrella as black clouds gather: it will PROBABLY rain.
fr_probablement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_completement_adv.hook: Like English 'completely', said kohn-pleh-tuh-MAHN: halfway through the debate an old councillor in a big white wig has fallen COMPLETELY asleep, eyes shut, chin on his hand.
fr_completement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_allemand_adj.hook: "Al, man!" ("ah-luh-MAHN") cries a pen pal from Berlin, waving a little GERMAN flag in the archives.
fr_allemand_adj.why: Painted live in the archives, not in an old photo.

fr_europeen_adj.hook: Like English 'European', said euh-roh-pay-AN: a girl files picture postcards from EUROPEAN places, a windmill and a leaning tower, into a long wooden drawer.
fr_europeen_adj.why: Stork replaced by a girl (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_francais_adj.hook: "France, eh?" ("frahn-SEH") says a visitor, opening a big FRENCH book tied with a blue-white-red ribbon.
fr_francais_adj.why: No text allowed, so the dictionary is a ribbon-tied book in French colors.

fr_local_adj.hook: Like English 'local', said loh-KAHL: the LOCAL baker gives a LOW CALL of "fresh bread!" through the archive window, holding up a basket of baguettes.
fr_local_adj.why: No line painted; the baker at the window carries the hook.

fr_etranger_adj.hook: A FOREIGN traveler with a sticker-covered suitcase walks into the archives: "Jay?" ("ay-trahn-ZHAY")
fr_etranger_adj.why: Painted arriving in the archives, not stepping off a train.

fr_belge_adj.hook: A BELGIAN waffle with a little black-yellow-red flag stuck on top.

fr_espagnol_adj.hook: A SPANISH spaniel ("ehs-pah-NYOL") dances flamenco on its hind legs, little bells ringing in its paws.
fr_espagnol_adj.why: The painted spaniel holds hand bells, not castanets.

fr_italien_adj.hook: Like English 'Italian', said ee-tah-LYAN: a gondolier named Ali, in a straw boater, sings an opera tune with an ITALIAN map rolled under his arm.
fr_italien_adj.why: Painted singing with the rolled map rather than filing it.

fr_parisien_adj.hook: Like English 'Parisian', said pah-ree-ZYAN: IAN in a navy coat holds up a PARISIAN postcard of the Eiffel Tower.
fr_parisien_adj.why: Striped sweater and beret removed (those belong to Monsieur Verbe).

fr_international_adj.hook: Like English 'international', said an-tehr-nah-syoh-NAHL: an archivist pins INTERNATIONAL picture postcards onto a big globe.
fr_international_adj.why: Stamps are too small to show; the postcards on the globe carry the hook.

fr_general_adj.hook: Like English 'general', said zhay-nay-RAHL: a GENERAL in medals sorts color-coded folders into one GENERAL drawer.
fr_general_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_mondial_adj.hook: A boy turns the "Mon" dial ("mohn-DYAHL") on a giant globe's stand to spin it WORLDWIDE.
fr_mondial_adj.why: The dial is painted on the stand with a boy turning it.

fr_national_adj.hook: Like English 'national', said nah-syoh-NAHL: an archivist folds a NATIONAL flag neatly into a box.
fr_national_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_particulier_adj.hook: Like English 'particular', said pahr-tee-kew-LYAY: a PARTY guest in a pointy hat is so PARTICULAR he lines up the archive shoe boxes by shoe size: "COOL, YAY!"
fr_particulier_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_politique_adj.hook: Like English 'political', said poh-lee-TEEK: POLLY the parrot squawks a POLITICAL speech from a carved TEAK podium.
fr_politique_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_africain_adj.hook: Like English 'African', said ah-free-KAN: an archivist holds up an AFRICAN map of the winding Nile, and a carved wooden giraffe stands close by.
fr_africain_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_americain_adj.hook: Like English 'American', said ah-may-ree-KAN: MARY files an AMERICAN map of the prairies and a postcard of a bison.
fr_americain_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_chinois_adj.hook: A CHINESE lantern glows over a little dragon as she ("shee-NWAH") waves a paper fan.
fr_chinois_adj.why: A dragon puppet stands in for the dragon parade.
fr_chinois_adj.note: 'C'est du chinois !' = it's all Greek to me. Never use it as a label for any Asian person.

fr_divers_adj.hook: Like English 'diverse', said dee-VEHR: VARIOUS objects spill out of an archive drawer: a compass, a feather, a key and a pair of DIVERS' flippers.
fr_divers_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_officiel_adj.hook: Like English 'official', said oh-fee-SYEHL: an OFFICIAL in a sash bangs a giant rubber stamp onto an archive paper.
fr_officiel_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_populaire_adj.hook: Like English 'popular', said poh-pew-LEHR: a fox family's LAIR under the map table is so POPULAR that children crowd round to peek in.
fr_populaire_adj.why: Real foxes (not anthropomorphic) and peeking children instead of autograph fans.

fr_royal_adj.hook: Like English 'royal', said rwah-YAHL: a ROYAL corgi in a tiny crown sits on a red velvet cushion.
fr_royal_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_social_adj.hook: Like English 'social', said soh-SYAHL: Uncle AL, very SOCIAL, chats cheerfully with everyone in line.
fr_social_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_liberte_noun.hook: Like English 'liberty', said lee-behr-TAY: a lady dressed as the Statue of LIBERTY raises her golden torch.

fr_societe_noun.hook: Like English 'society', said soh-syay-TAY: the ladies of the flower-hat SOCIETY pose proudly for their club portrait.
fr_societe_noun.why: Club ladies in flowered hats painted.

fr_population_noun.hook: Like English 'population', said poh-pew-lah-SYOHN: balloons POP as a lady clicks her counter to count the town's POPULATION.

fr_association_noun.hook: A SOCK for every member: a lady hands out matching striped socks to her club, the 'ah-SOCK-see-ah-syohn' (ASSOCIATION).

fr_union_noun.hook: Sounds like ONION ('ew-NYOHN'): a lady holds a giant onion tied with a ribbon, the sign of the UNION.
fr_union_noun.why: Giant onion with a ribbon painted.

fr_independance_noun.hook: IN-DEPENDANCE = dancing on her own: a girl twirls a ribbon and dances all by herself, full of INDEPENDENCE.

fr_communaute_noun.hook: Like English 'community', said koh-mew-noh-TAY: neighbors water a shared COMMUNITY vegetable planter together.

fr_egal_adj.hook: Two GALs ('ay-GAHL') sit perfectly level on a seesaw: EQUAL weight, EQUAL height.

fr_communiste_noun.hook: Like English 'communist', said koh-mew-NEEST: a man in a worker's flat cap waves a plain red flag toward a painted sunrise.
fr_communiste_noun.why: Red flag, flat cap; no symbols or text.

fr_droit_noun.hook: 'DRAW-ah!' ('drwah'): a man raises his RIGHT hand high with a giant pencil, ready to DRAW, claiming his RIGHT.
fr_droit_noun.why: Raised right hand with giant pencil.

fr_membre_noun.hook: Like English 'member', said MAHM-bruh: a proud MEMBER shows off his blank membership card and rosette.
fr_membre_noun.why: Blank card with rosette; no text.
fr_membre_noun.note: In anatomy it can also mean the male organ; the context makes it clear.

fr_refuge_noun.hook: Like English 'refuge', said ruh-FEWZH: a man holds an umbrella over a leaky little shelter so the kittens have a REFUGE from the rain.

fr_clan_noun.hook: Like English 'clan', said KLAHN: three men in matching red plaid kilts, one family CLAN.

fr_esclavage_noun.hook: L'ESCLAVAGE ('ess-klah-VAHZH', slavery): a sensitive word, so it is not drawn. It sits on a plain blank museum plaque on a roped-off marble pedestal; the word itself is the hook.
fr_esclavage_noun.why: Mature/sensitive word: museum-style blank plaque, word shown only as the HTML label; velvet rope = neutral 'exhibit' cue.
fr_esclavage_noun.note: A heavy historical subject (France abolished slavery in 1848), so use it with care.

fr_manifestation_noun.hook: LA MANIFESTATION ('mah-nee-fess-tah-SYOHN'): MANY FEST! Many festive marchers parade with blank placards on sticks and a big drum.
fr_manifestation_noun.why: Sound-alike MANY + FEST: a cheerful crowd marching with placards = a demonstration.

fr_pauvrete_noun.hook: LA PAUVRETÉ ('poh-vruh-TAY', poverty): a sensitive word, so it is not drawn. It sits on a plain blank framed plaque on a low wooden stand; the word itself is the hook.
fr_pauvrete_noun.why: Grave/sensitive word: museum-style blank plaque, word shown only as the HTML label.

fr_commune_noun.hook: LA COMMUNE ('koh-MUEN'): COMMON! A man proudly holds a model of his little village built around its green COMMON, with one toy cow grazing.
fr_commune_noun.why: Sound-alike COMMON: a village round its common = the commune (smallest French local district).

fr_solidarite_noun.hook: LA SOLIDARITÉ ('soh-lee-dah-ree-TAY'): SOLID! Four friends link arms and stand together on one big SOLID granite block.
fr_solidarite_noun.why: Sound-alike SOLID: standing together, arms linked, on solid rock = solidarity.

fr_tribu_noun.hook: LA TRIBU ('tree-BUE'): TREE-BOO! A whole three-generation family, grandparents to kids, pops out from behind a potted TREE shouting BOO!
fr_tribu_noun.why: Sound-alike TREE + BOO; a big extended family group = a tribe (no costume shorthand).

fr_foire_noun.hook: LA FOIRE ('FWAHR'): FOUR! A girl carries a toy fair merry-go-round with exactly FOUR little horses.
fr_foire_noun.why: Sound-alike FOUR; the merry-go-round = a fair. Count: 4 horses.

fr_generosite_noun.hook: LA GÉNÉROSITÉ ('zhay-nay-roh-zee-TAY'): GENEROUS CITY! A boy hands his whole big fruit pie to another boy to share.
fr_generosite_noun.why: Sound-alike GENEROUS + CITY: giving away the whole pie = generosity.

fr_egalite_noun.hook: L'ÉGALITÉ ('ay-gah-lee-TAY'): EGG-ALITY! A brass scale hangs perfectly LEVEL with one identical white EGG in each pan.
fr_egalite_noun.why: Sound-alike EGG; equal eggs, level scale = equality. Its twin l'inégalité is the tipped scale next to it.

fr_inegalite_noun.hook: L'INÉGALITÉ ('ee-nay-gah-lee-TAY'): IN-EGG-ALITY! The second scale is steeply TIPPED: one huge EGG sinks low, one tiny egg flies high.
fr_inegalite_noun.why: Sound-alike EGG; near-synonym cue: tipped scale with unequal eggs vs the level scale of l'égalité.

fr_participation_noun.hook: LA PARTICIPATION ('par-tee-see-pah-SYOHN'): PARTY! A boy in a pointed PARTY hat shoots his hand up, eager to join in.
fr_participation_noun.why: Sound-alike PARTY: hand up to take part = participation.

fr_surement_adv.hook: Said sew-ruh-MAHN: a SURE-footed mountain goat SURELY strolls along the top of the council benches.
fr_surement_adv.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: removed 'Like English X' (not a cognate).

fr_vraiment_adv.hook: A donkey BRAYS at a MAN ("vreh-MAHN") with raised eyebrows: "REALLY? REALLY?!"
fr_vraiment_adv.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (vray-MON) -> (vreh-MAHN) to match the card.

fr_cependant_adv.hook: "HOWEVER hungry you are, DAN, the SAUCEPAN ("suh-pahn-DAHN") is empty!", HOWEVER, there is a cookie.
fr_cependant_adv.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (suh-pon-DON) -> (suh-pahn-DAHN) to match the card.

fr_poubelle_noun.hook: The big green TRASH CAN has a BELL on its lid that rings every time you throw something in: pou-BELLE! (It is named after Monsieur Poubelle, who brought trash cans to Paris.)
fr_poubelle_noun.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_file_noun.hook: Three EELS wait patiently in a LINE at the town hall, the first one holding its ticket. Eel... FEEL! La file is the line.
fr_file_noun.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_colis_noun.hook: A fluffy COLLIE dog proudly carries the PACKAGE in its mouth: koh-LEE = collie.
fr_colis_noun.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_mairie_noun.hook: "may-REE": a bride and groom who have just come to MARRY at the TOWN HALL cut their wedding cake: MARRY
fr_mairie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a smiling bride in a white dress and a groom in a gray suit cutting a three-tier white wedding cake together, rose petals scattered on the floor.
fr_mairie_noun.note: La mairie is the town hall of a commune; in France every civil wedding takes place there, in front of the mayor.

fr_accorder_verb.hook: "ah-kor-DAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret), an ACCORDION strapped to his chest, GRANTS the newlyweds the big gold key of the town, tied with a red bow: A-CORD-AY: ACCORDION
fr_accorder_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, standing on a low wooden step with a red accordion strapped on his chest, holding out a big gold key with a red bow toward the wedding couple, his other hand raised in a flourish.
fr_accorder_verb.note: Accorder means to grant or to give (accorder une faveur, accorder dix minutes); it also means to tune an instrument (accorder un piano). S'accorder: to agree, or to go well together (des couleurs qui s'accordent).

fr_ministre_noun.hook: "mee-NEESTR": a stately MINISTER in a dark suit sips punch through a teeny MINI STRAW from a tall punch glass: MINI-STRAW
fr_ministre_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a tall gray-haired woman minister in a dark navy suit sipping pink punch from a tall glass through a tiny mini drinking straw.
fr_ministre_noun.note: Un ministre heads a government department; the word is masculine or feminine (le/la ministre). Not a church minister: that is un pasteur.

fr_president_noun.hook: "pray-zee-DAHN": everyone PRAISES DON, the club PRESIDENT, who blushes and lifts a gold trophy cup over his head: PRAISE-E-DON
fr_president_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a round-faced man with a gray mustache and a gold chain of office around his neck lifting a big gold trophy cup over his head, blushing, two guests beside him clapping.
fr_president_noun.note: Président also means the chair of a club, a meeting or a company (le président du club).

fr_depute_noun.hook: "day-pew-TAY": a DEPUTY in a suit with a tricolor sash taps a golf PUTT across the parquet toward a little golf hole on a green felt mat: DAY-PUTT-AY
fr_depute_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a young man with a short beard in a dark suit and a blue-white-red sash across his chest, crouched over a golf putter, tapping a white golf ball across the parquet floor toward a little golf cup hole in a small green felt putting mat.
fr_depute_noun.note: Un député is an elected member of the Assemblée nationale (a member of Parliament, like a U.S. representative), not a sheriff's deputy.

fr_ministere_noun.hook: "mee-nees-TEHR": on a round table stands a big model of the MINISTRY, and a little boy walks two fingers up its MINI STAIRcase: MINI-STAIR
fr_ministere_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a big white scale model of a grand columned government building with a wide sweeping mini staircase, on a round table, a little boy walking two fingers up the tiny stairs.
fr_ministere_noun.note: Un ministère is a government department and its building (le ministère de la Culture).

fr_congres_noun.hook: "kohn-GREH": a waiter brings a tray of GRAY ice-cream CONES to the CONGRESS delegates, who stare at the strange gray scoops: CONE-GRAY
fr_congres_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a waiter in a white jacket holding up a silver tray of five ice-cream cones with gray scoops, two delegates in suits with lanyards peering at them in surprise.
fr_congres_noun.note: Un congrès is a large formal meeting or conference (un congrès de médecins); in the U.S., le Congrès is Congress.

fr_signature_noun.hook: "see-nyah-TEWR": a TOUR guide holding up a little yellow pennant signs her name with a big swirly SIGNATURE while her tourists in sun hats wave 'SEE YA!': SEE-YA-TOUR
fr_signature_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a woman tour guide holding up a small yellow pennant on a stick in one hand and signing a large sheet of paper on a standing desk with the other, two tourists in sun hats and cameras on straps waving goodbye.
fr_signature_noun.note: La signature is both your signature and the act of signing (la signature du contrat).

fr_demarche_noun.hook: "day-MAHRSH": a man with an armful of forms MARCHES like a drum major from counter to counter, knees high: the long DÉMARCHE (process): DAY-MARCH
fr_demarche_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a man in a brown cardigan marching with high knees like a drum major, a big armful of papers held to his chest, crossing the floor between two counters.
fr_demarche_noun.note: Also means a person's walk or gait (une démarche élégante) and a step taken to get something done (faire des démarches).

fr_dossier_noun.hook: "doh-SYAY": a young DOE pokes her head over the counter and nibbles the corner of a fat DOSSIER (file) a clerk holds out: DOE-SEE-AY
fr_dossier_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a young spotted deer doe poking her head over the wooden counter and nibbling the corner of a thick tan cardboard file folder that a surprised clerk with glasses is holding.
fr_dossier_noun.note: Second sense: the back of a chair (le dossier de la chaise).

fr_sceau_noun.hook: "SOH": a gray-haired lady SEWS a red ribbon onto the document while the clerk beside her presses a brass SEAL into a blob of red wax on it: SEW
fr_sceau_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a gray-haired lady with glasses in a lilac cardigan sewing a ribbon onto a large paper with a needle and thread, and beside her a young clerk in a blue cardigan pressing a brass seal stamp into a blob of red wax with a red ribbon on the same paper.
fr_sceau_noun.note: Same sound as seau (bucket), saut (jump) and sot (fool): only the spelling sceau means seal.

fr_document_noun.hook: "doh-kew-MAHN": a DOCtor in a white coat points with a billiard CUE at the notice board where the important DOCUMENTs go: DOC-CUE-MAN
fr_document_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a doctor in a white coat with a stethoscope pointing with a long wooden billiard cue at a big cork notice board.
fr_document_noun.note: Like English document; also a computer file (un document Word).

fr_permis_noun.hook: "pehr-MEE": a freckled teenage boy with a fresh curly red PERM, still in pink rollers, proudly holds up his new driver's PERMIT: PERM-ME
fr_permis_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a grinning freckled red-haired teenage boy in a green sweater, his fresh curly perm still in pink rollers, holding up a small pink card.
fr_permis_noun.note: Le permis de conduire is a driver's license; un permis de construire is a building permit.

fr_pancarte_noun.hook: "pahn-KAHRT": a cook pushes a CART full of shiny frying PANS, and a big blank PLACARD on a pole sticks up out of it: PAN-CART
fr_pancarte_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a cheerful cook in a white apron pushing a wooden hand cart piled with shiny copper frying pans, a big blank white placard on a tall wooden pole standing up out of the cart.
fr_pancarte_noun.note: Une pancarte is any sign or placard: a notice on a door or a sign carried in a march.

fr_banderole_noun.hook: "bahn-duh-ROL": a little marching BAND plays under the long blank BANNER they have just unROLLed across the hall: BAND-A-ROLL
fr_banderole_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): two band musicians in red jackets and bowler hats, a trumpeter and a drummer, playing under a long blank white cloth banner hung between two poles.
fr_banderole_noun.note: Une banderole is a long banner carried in a march or hung up at a match.

fr_voter_verb.hook: "voh-TAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) VOTES, dropping his envelope into the clear ballot box while balancing a cup of TEA on its saucer in his other hand: VOTE-TEA
fr_voter_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, standing at the table dropping a small blue envelope into a clear plastic ballot box with one hand, holding a teacup on a saucer in his other hand.
fr_voter_verb.note: Voter pour quelqu'un = to vote for someone. Une voix is a vote cast.

fr_partisan_noun.hook: "pahr-tee-ZAHN": a cheering SUPPORTER waves a giant wedge of PARMESAN cheese over his head like a foam finger: PARMESAN
fr_partisan_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a cheering young man with a blue-white-red rosette on his sweater waving a giant yellow wedge of parmesan cheese over his head.
fr_partisan_noun.note: Un partisan is a supporter of an idea or a person (un partisan du vélo). It is not party-political in the English sense of 'partisan'; in history it also means a resistance fighter.

fr_electeur_noun.hook: "ay-lehk-TUHR": an elderly VOTER in line gives A LECTURE to a bored teenager, wagging a finger, ballot envelope in hand: A-LECTURE
fr_electeur_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): an elderly woman voter with a white bun and a handbag wagging her finger and lecturing a bored teenage boy who rolls his eyes, both standing in line by the voting booths, she holds a small blue envelope.
fr_electeur_noun.note: Une électrice is a woman voter. La carte d'électeur is the voter card.

fr_elu_noun.hook: "ay-LEW": two friends lift LOU, the newly ELECTED official, onto their shoulders, and the crowd shouts 'HEY, LOU!': HEY-LOU
fr_elu_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a beaming man in a suit lifted onto the shoulders of two laughing friends, waving both arms in victory.
fr_elu_noun.note: Un élu is any elected official (les élus municipaux); as an adjective, élu means elected or chosen.

fr_payant_adj.hook: "peh-YAHN": at the door a visitor PAYS for his ticket and the cashier gives an enormous YAWN: entry is PAYANT (not free): PAY-YAWN
fr_payant_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): at a small ticket table a man handing over a coin to a cashier lady who is yawning hugely with her hand near her mouth, a cash tin on the table.
fr_payant_adj.note: Payant means you have to pay (le parking est payant); the opposite is gratuit, free. Of a job or business: paying, profitable.

fr_rentable_adj.hook: "rahn-TAHBL": a beekeeper lady pays to RENT A TABLE at the fair and stacks it with honey jars that sell fast: PROFITABLE: RENT-A-TABLE
fr_rentable_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a beekeeper lady in a straw hat stacking golden honey jars on a trestle table, a man in an apron taking a coin from her for the table, a little pile of coins in a dish.
fr_rentable_adj.note: Rentable means profitable or worth it (un investissement rentable); it comes from la rente, income, not from English 'rent'.

fr_benevole_adj.hook: "bay-nay-VOL": BENNY, a VOLUNTEER in a green apron, keeps a beach ball going in a VOLLEY with the children, unpaid and happy: BENNY-VOLLEY
fr_benevole_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a cheerful young man in a green apron hitting a big striped beach ball up into the air in a volley, two small children reaching up for it.
fr_benevole_adj.note: Also a noun: un or une bénévole is a volunteer (unpaid helper).

fr_fierement_adv.hook: "fyeh-ruh-MAHN": a FIREMAN in his shiny helmet stands PROUDLY with his chest out and a new medal on his jacket: FIRE-MAN
fr_fierement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a firefighter in a dark blue uniform and a shiny silver helmet standing proudly with his chest out and hands on his hips, a round gold medal pinned on his jacket.
fr_fierement_adv.note: Fièrement comes from fier, proud (fier de son travail).

fr_paisiblement_adv.hook: "pay-zee-bluh-MAHN": an old man in a PAISLEY BLUE shirt dozes PEACEFULLY in a folding chair up on the stage: PAISLEY-BLUE-MAN
fr_paisiblement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): an old man with white hair in a blue paisley-patterned shirt dozing peacefully in a wooden folding chair up on the stage, his hands folded on his belly, eyes closed and a small smile.
fr_paisiblement_adv.note: Paisiblement comes from paisible, peaceful (from la paix, peace).

fr_carrement_adv.hook: "kah-ray-MAHN": a strongman CARRIES a whole upright piano across the hall in his arms: carrément, really, the WHOLE thing!: CARRY-MAN
fr_carrement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a burly strongman with a curly mustache, in a sleeveless blue shirt, hugging a whole brown upright piano in his arms and carrying it across the hall, grinning.
fr_carrement_adv.note: Carrément is informal: 'totally, really' (c'est carrément génial) or 'bluntly, straight out' (il me l'a dit carrément).

fr_apparemment_adv.hook: "ah-pah-rah-MAHN": APPARENTLY a pirate? No: it is just the mailman, A PARROT, MAN, perched on his shoulder, delivering a parcel: A-PARROT-MAN
fr_apparemment_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/polyvalente (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a friendly mailman in a light-blue shirt and cap with a big green parrot perched on his shoulder, holding out a brown parcel.
fr_apparemment_adv.note: Apparemment means apparently, seemingly: it reports what things look like (Apparemment, il pleut). It also works as a careful 'it seems so' answer. It never means 'clearly' (that is évidemment).

fr_nullement_adv.hook: "new-luh-MAHN": a little boy offers his big sister a shiny NEW LEMON, and she puckers and shakes her head: NOT AT ALL, thanks!: NEW-LEMON
fr_nullement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/polyvalente (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a little boy holding up a big shiny lemon to his sister, who crosses her arms and shakes her head. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_nullement_adv.note: Nullement is a formal, emphatic 'not at all, in no way' (Je ne suis nullement fâché = I'm not at all angry). It needs ne in a full sentence; alone it answers 'Not in the least.' It is the negative of an idea, so it never means 'nullified'.

fr_insister_verb.hook: "an-sees-TAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) INSISTS, waving his shy SISTER, peeking from the stage curtain with her ukulele, IN: 'IN, SISTER!' (an-sees-TAY): IN-SISTER
fr_insister_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/polyvalente (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, standing on the low stage, beckoning with both hands to a shy young woman holding a ukulele who hides half behind the side of the gray backdrop. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg007 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_insister_verb.note: Insister means to insist (Il insiste pour payer) and also to stress a point (insister sur un détail). N'insiste pas! = Drop it! Don't push it.

fr_proprement_adv.hook: "pro-pruh-MAHN": the PROP MAN in overalls lines up the stage props neatly and PROPERLY on a long shelf: a paper crown, a lantern, a toy horse: PROP-MAN
fr_proprement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/polyvalente (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a tidy stagehand in gray overalls and a flat cap carefully lining up props in a neat row on a long wooden shelf beside the stage: a gold paper crown, a brass lantern and a toy rocking horse. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_proprement_adv.note: Proprement means properly, decently (Mange proprement!) and also cleanly, neatly. À proprement parler = strictly speaking. Not 'proper' in the sense of 'own' (that is propre placed before the noun: ma propre chambre).

fr_veritablement_adv.hook: "vay-ree-tah-bluh-MAHN": a small round man carries a VERY long TABLE on his head across the room: it is TRULY enormous!: VERY-TABLE-MAN
fr_veritablement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/polyvalente (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a short round cheerful man in a red sweater balancing an extremely long wooden trestle table on his head, both ends sticking far out, arms up holding it, tongue out in concentration. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_03_z1 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_veritablement_adv.note: Véritablement means truly, genuinely (un film véritablement drôle). A stronger, more literary word than vraiment.

fr_totalement_adv.hook: "toh-tah-luh-MAHN": a helper comes in with TOTE bags hanging ALL over him, ten on each arm and one in his teeth: TOTALLY loaded: TOTE-ALL-MAN
fr_totalement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/polyvalente (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a lanky young man in a green cardigan with many colorful cloth tote bags hanging all along both arms and around his neck, one tote bag handle held in his teeth.
fr_totalement_adv.note: Totalement means totally, completely (Je suis totalement d'accord). Pas totalement = not completely.

fr_catalan_adj.hook: "kah-tah-LAHN": a ginger CAT naps on A little square of green LAWN on a small table, wearing a red-and-yellow striped CATALAN scarf: CAT-A-LAWN
fr_catalan_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/jumelage (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a ginger cat in a red-and-yellow striped scarf napping on a little square of green lawn on a small table.
fr_catalan_adj.note: Catalan describes Catalonia, the region around Barcelona (and the French Pays catalan around Perpignan); le catalan is also its language. Capitalize only the noun for a person: un Catalan, une Catalane.

fr_flamand_adj.hook: "flah-MAHN": a FLEMISH baker with a white lace collar, like a man in an old Flemish painting, holds up a huge wobbling caramel FLAN: the FLAN MAN: FLAN-MAN
fr_flamand_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/jumelage (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a plump baker dressed like a man in an old Flemish painting, black tunic and a wide white pleated lace collar, holding up a huge wobbling golden caramel flan on a plate.
fr_flamand_adj.note: Flamand means Flemish, from Flanders (in Belgium and the far north of France); le flamand is also the language. Same sound as flamant, the flamingo (un flamant rose): only the last letter differs.

fr_rassembler_verb.hook: "rah-sahn-BLAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) shakes maracas and GATHERS everyone into a SAMBA line: RA-SAMBA-LAY!: RA-SAMBA-LAY
fr_rassembler_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/jumelage (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, shaking two maracas and dancing, leading a happy line of guests holding each other's shoulders. Moved from the planned room ST_making_seg005 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_rassembler_verb.note: Rassembler means to gather, assemble (rassembler ses affaires = to gather your things; rassembler son courage = to summon up your courage). Se rassembler = to gather, meet up. Not the same as ressembler (to look like).

fr_bresilien_adj.hook: "bray-zee-LYAN": a big friendly LION mascot in a yellow soccer jersey dances the samba: the BRAZIL LION: BRAZIL-LION
fr_bresilien_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/jumelage (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a lion mascot in a yellow soccer jersey dancing the samba. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_05 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_bresilien_adj.note: Brésilien means Brazilian (la musique brésilienne); un Brésilien, une Brésilienne is a person from Brazil (le Brésil).

fr_fameux_adj.hook: "fah-MEUH": a FAMOUS cow in a flower garland poses on a little red rug while a photographer snaps her picture, and she MOOs: FA-MOO!: FA-MOO
fr_fameux_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/jumelage (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a cow in a flower garland posing on a red rug for a photographer. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_05 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_fameux_adj.note: Fameux means famous, well-known; before a noun it also means 'great, excellent' (un fameux repas). Ironic in Ce n'est pas fameux = it's not great.

fr_cosmopolite_adj.hook: "kos-moh-poh-LEET": a very POLITE COSMOnaut in his space suit bows deeply to the guests from everywhere: COSMO-POLITE: COSMO-POLITE
fr_cosmopolite_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/jumelage (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a white-suited astronaut bowing politely. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_07 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_cosmopolite_adj.note: Cosmopolite means cosmopolitan: a city or person mixing many cultures (une ville cosmopolite).

fr_ambassade_noun.hook: "ahn-bah-SAHD": a big BASS fish sits in a washtub and proudly holds up its own passport while a clerk stamps it: the EMBASSY has sorted its papers: AM-BASS-ADE
fr_ambassade_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/jumelage (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a big green bass fish sitting upright in a wooden washtub of water, holding up a small red passport in its fin, a clerk lady at the left edge stamping it. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_ambassade_noun.note: Une ambassade is an embassy (l'ambassade de France à Washington). In formal or historical French it is also an official mission, a delegation sent to a ruler. The person is un ambassadeur, une ambassadrice.

fr_fiche_noun.hook: "FEESH": a clerk hands a man his FORM card back, and a slippery silver FISH is flopping right on top of it: FISH
fr_fiche_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/etatcivil (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a surprised man in a beige raincoat reaching for a white index card that a clerk holds out across the counter, a slippery silver fish flopping on top of the card. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z2 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_fiche_noun.note: Une fiche is an index card, a form or record card (remplir une fiche = fill in a form; une fiche de paie = a pay stub). It is also an electric plug. Not a fish: that is un poisson.

fr_licence_noun.hook: "lee-SAHNS": little LEE proudly shows the clerk his glass ant farm: LEE'S ANTS now have an official LICENSE card: LEE'S-ANTS
fr_licence_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/etatcivil (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a proud little boy with glasses holding up a glass ant farm full of tunnels and tiny ants, a small plain card taped to its side, an old clerk smiling at it. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z2 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_licence_noun.note: Une licence is a license or permit (une licence de taxi); it is also a sports club membership card and, at a university, a bachelor's degree (une licence d'histoire). French spells it with c only.

fr_gestion_noun.hook: "zhehs-TYOHN": at the manager's desk piled with ledgers, a JESTER in a belled hat gives a huge YAWN: MANAGEMENT bores him to tears: JEST-YAWN
fr_gestion_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/etatcivil (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a jester in a red-and-yellow belled jester hat and costume sitting at a desk piled with ledgers and papers, stretching and giving a huge yawn. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z2 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_gestion_noun.note: La gestion is management, administration (la gestion d'une entreprise; la gestion du temps). Mauvaise gestion = mismanagement. Not a gesture (un geste).

fr_autoriser_verb.hook: "oh-toh-ree-ZAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) gives a thumbs-up and AUTHORIZES the shiny toy AUTO to RISE on its little lift: AUTO-RISE-AY
fr_autoriser_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/etatcivil (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, giving a big thumbs-up while a shiny red child's pedal car rises up on a small yellow scissor lift beside him. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg002 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_autoriser_verb.note: Autoriser means to authorize, to allow (autoriser quelqu'un à partir). Non autorisé = unauthorized; s'autoriser quelque chose = to treat yourself to it.

fr_label_noun.hook: "lah-BEHL": a clerk polishes LA big brass BELL, which wears a round gold quality LABEL sticker: LA-BELL
fr_label_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/etatcivil (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a big shiny brass bell on a wooden stand with a round plain gold sticker on it, a young clerk in a vest polishing it with a cloth.
fr_label_noun.note: Un label is a quality label or seal of approval (un label bio = an organic label) and also a record label. A plain sticky label or tag is une étiquette.

fr_tampon_noun.hook: "tahn-POHN": TOM the clerk plays PING-PONG across the counter, using a big RUBBER STAMP as his paddle: TOM-PONG
fr_tampon_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/etatcivil (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a lanky young clerk with red hair hitting a white ping-pong ball with a big wooden-handled rubber stamp used as a paddle, the ball in the air. Moved from the planned room R_admin_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_tampon_noun.note: Un tampon is a rubber stamp (and its ink pad); it is also a buffer or plug, a cotton pad, and a feminine hygiene tampon. Tamponner = to stamp, or to bump into another car.

fr_statut_noun.hook: "stah-TEW": a white marble STATUE has come to life by the window and points at the little tally scoreboard on the wall to check her STATUS: STATUE
fr_statut_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/etatcivil (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a white marble statue of a robed woman on a low plinth by the window, pointing at a small dark green board of white tally marks on the wall. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z1 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_statut_noun.note: Le statut is a status, a standing (le statut social; le statut marital on a form: single, married…) and, often in the plural, the statutes or bylaws of a club or company (les statuts d'une association). Careful: a statue is la statue, feminine, and sounds almost the same.

fr_monetaire_adj.hook: "moh-nay-TEHR": a scruffy MONEY TERRIER dashes off with paper money in his mouth while the treasurer chases him: MONEY-TERRIER
fr_monetaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/finances (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a scruffy little terrier dog running with a fat bundle of green paper banknotes in its mouth, a bald treasurer in a waistcoat chasing it with arms out.
fr_monetaire_adj.note: Monétaire means monetary, to do with money and currency (la politique monétaire, une unité monétaire). Money itself is l'argent or la monnaie.

fr_prospere_adj.hook: "pros-PEHR": two proud farmers present a giant golden PEAR on a cushion: the PROSPEROUS harvest of a PROSPEROUS village: PROS-PEAR
fr_prospere_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/finances (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): two proud farmers in their Sunday best presenting a giant golden pear as big as a pumpkin on a red velvet cushion.
fr_prospere_adj.note: Prospère means prosperous, thriving (une ville prospère). Its opposite is pauvre or en déclin; prospérer = to thrive.

fr_reclamer_verb.hook: "ray-klah-MAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) holds out his hand and DEMANDS his CLAM back from a cheeky seagull on the windowsill: RE-CLAM-AY
fr_reclamer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/finances (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, leaning toward the open back window with one hand held out flat, demanding, while a cheeky white seagull on the windowsill holds a clam in its beak. Moved from the planned room ST_conflict_seg010 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_reclamer_verb.note: Réclamer means to claim, demand, ask for something back (réclamer un remboursement). It also means to complain (une réclamation = a complaint). Not 'reclaim land' (that is assécher).

fr_minier_adj.hook: "mee-NYAY": a boy shouts 'YAY!' at a model of the old MINING town on a table, with MINI miners in tiny helmets: MINI-YAY
fr_minier_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/finances (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a boy cheering with both arms up beside a big table model of an old mining town with a wooden mine tower, tiny rail carts and tiny miner figures in helmets.
fr_minier_adj.note: Minier means mining (une ville minière, l'industrie minière, un bassin minier). Not 'minor' (that is mineur, which also means a miner).

fr_annuel_adj.hook: "ah-NWEHL": on top of the safe, AN OWL blows out the single candle on its cupcake: its ANNUAL birthday: AN-OWL
fr_annuel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/finances (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a round brown owl sitting on top of the iron safe blowing out a single candle on a pink cupcake. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_06 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_annuel_adj.note: Annuel means annual, yearly (la fête annuelle). Un abonnement annuel = a yearly subscription; it is also a yearbook or annual publication (un annuel).

fr_apport_noun.hook: "ah-POR": a smiling grandmother does A big POUR of coins from her jug into the glass jar: her CONTRIBUTION: A-POUR
fr_apport_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/finances (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a smiling grandmother in a blue dress pouring a stream of gold coins from a pottery jug into a big glass jar on a desk. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_apport_noun.note: Un apport is a contribution, input (l'apport de chacun; un apport personnel = a down payment on a home). Food labels: l'apport en fer = iron intake.

fr_equite_noun.hook: "ay-kee-TAY": on the desk, a brass balance scale holds A KITTY in each pan, and the pans stay perfectly level: perfectly FAIR: A-KITTY
fr_equite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/finances (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a brass balance scale on the desk with one small kitten sitting in each pan, the two pans exactly level. Moved from the planned room R_society_04 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_equite_noun.note: L'équité is fairness, equity: treating people fairly (en toute équité = in all fairness). In finance, equity in a company is les capitaux propres, not l'équité. Its opposite is l'injustice or l'iniquité.

fr_elire_verb.hook: "ay-LEER": perched on top of the voting booths, MONSIEUR VERBE (gold beret) gives his ballot A sly LEER, rubbing his chin as he decides whom to ELECT: A-LEER
fr_elire_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a gold beret, little motion lines around his hands, sitting on top of the voting booths holding up a white ballot paper, giving it a comical sly leer: one eyebrow arched, half-lidded eyes glancing sideways, a crooked smirk, one hand rubbing his chin. Moved from the planned room ST_rule_seg003 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_elire_verb.note: Élire means to elect (élire un maire). It is irregular like lire: j'élis, nous élisons, j'ai élu. Un élu, une élue is an elected official. Élire domicile is formal for 'to take up residence'.

fr_candidat_noun.hook: "kahn-dee-DAH": on the campaign poster, a grinning CANDIDATE pulls a giant CANDY cane out of a top hat: ta-DAH!: CANDY-DAH
fr_candidat_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): a framed campaign poster of a grinning man in a navy suit with a tricolor rosette pulling a giant red-and-white candy cane out of a black top hat. Moved from the planned room R_politics_01 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_candidat_noun.note: Un candidat, une candidate is a candidate in an election (être candidat à la mairie = to run for mayor) and also an applicant for a job or someone taking an exam (les candidats au bac). Un candidat malheureux is a losing candidate.

fr_valider_verb.hook: "vah-lee-DAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) VALIDATES a postcard of a sunny green VALLEY by DAY, drawing a big green check mark across it: VALLEY-DAY
fr_valider_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, holding up a postcard of a green valley under a bright sun and drawing a big green check mark across it with a marker. Moved from the planned room ST_rule_seg012 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_valider_verb.note: Valider means to validate, to approve or confirm (valider un paiement = confirm a payment; valider son ticket = stamp a ticket in the machine; valider un diplôme or a course = pass it). Informally, Je valide ! means I approve! The opposite is invalider or refuser.

fr_declarer_verb.hook: "day-klah-RAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) holds a CLARINET high and DECLARES to the whole hall: 'Today is CLARINET DAY!': DAY-CLAR(inet)
fr_declarer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, standing on the parquet among the rose petals, holding a black clarinet high above his head with one hand, his other hand raised in an announcing gesture, mouth open in a proud declaration. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg003 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_declarer_verb.note: Déclarer means to declare or announce (déclarer son amour) and to report something officially: déclarer une naissance = register a birth, déclarer ses revenus = file your income taxes, déclarer un vol = report a theft. Se déclarer: a fire or illness breaks out (un incendie s'est déclaré).

fr_agence_noun.hook: "ah-ZHAHNS": a smiling travel-AGENCY lady zooms a toy airplane across a big desk map for a young couple planning their trip: an AGENCY arranges things for you: AGENCY
fr_agence_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a smiling woman in a teal blazer at a small desk zooming a white toy airplane across a big blank-colored desk map, a young couple leaning in, delighted.
fr_agence_noun.note: Une agence is an agency or office (une agence de voyages = travel agency; une agence immobilière = real-estate agency; une agence bancaire = bank branch). The person is un agent, une agente. Not to be confused with l'agenda (a diary or planner).

fr_identite_noun.hook: "ee-dahn-tee-TAY": at the counter a puzzled clerk looks from one twin brother to the other: two IDENTICAL faces, so whose IDENTITY is whose?: IDENTITY
fr_identite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): identical twin brothers in matching green sweaters standing side by side at the counter grinning, a puzzled clerk behind it looking from one to the other and scratching her head.
fr_identite_noun.note: L'identité is identity (une carte d'identité = an ID card; une pièce d'identité = any photo ID; un contrôle d'identité = an ID check). Une erreur d'identité is mistaken identity. Like English, it can also mean sameness (l'identité de deux choses).

fr_administratif_adj.hook: "ahd-mee-nees-trah-TEEF": a frazzled clerk balances a teetering ADMINISTRATIVE tower of paper forms on her desk: ADMINISTRATIVE
fr_administratif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a frazzled young clerk with her hair coming loose at the far counter, steadying a teetering tower of blank paper forms taller than she is with both hands. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z2 into this room.
fr_administratif_adj.note: Administratif means administrative (les démarches administratives = official paperwork; un centre administratif = government offices). Masc. administratif, fem. administrative. Le personnel administratif is the office staff; la paperasse administrative is red tape.

fr_confirmer_verb.hook: "kohn-feer-MAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) CONFIRMS the appointment with a big FIRM handshake across the counter, nodding hard: yes, it's settled!: CONFIRM (a FIRM handshake)
fr_confirmer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, leaning over the counter giving a firm, pumping handshake to a smiling woman with a handbag, both nodding. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg008 into this room.
fr_confirmer_verb.note: Confirmer means to confirm (confirmer un rendez-vous, une réservation) and, of a court, to uphold a decision (confirmer un jugement). Se confirmer is to be confirmed (La nouvelle se confirme). The opposite is démentir or infirmer (to deny, to overturn).

fr_convoquer_verb.hook: "CONVOY-KAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) beckons a little CONVOY of children on ride-on toy trucks to come in: he SUMMONS them (kohn-voh-KAY): CONVOY-KAY
fr_convoquer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, beckoning with both white-gloved hands to three small children riding in a line of red ride-on toy trucks rolling toward him. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg012 into this room.
fr_convoquer_verb.note: Convoquer means to summon or call someone in officially (être convoqué à la mairie, au commissariat, à un entretien) and to convene a meeting (convoquer une assemblée). Une convocation is the official letter calling you in. It never means to convoy; that is escorter or convoyer.

fr_arrondissement_noun.hook: "ah-rohn-dee-suh-MAHN": on the wall, a big map of Paris whose districts spiral out like a snail shell, and a real garden snail crawls along the spiral of ARRONDISSEMENTS: SNAIL MAP
fr_arrondissement_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a big wall map of a city divided into colored patches that spiral outward like a snail shell, a big garden snail crawling along the spiral, a clerk tracing it with a finger.
fr_arrondissement_noun.note: Un arrondissement is a district of a big city: Paris, Lyon and Marseille are divided into numbered arrondissements (j'habite dans le 11e). It is also a subdivision of a French département. Arrondir means to round off, and l'arrondissement is also the rounding of a number.

fr_departement_noun.hook: "day-pahr-tuh-MAHN": a boy presses the last puzzle piece into a big jigsaw map of France: each piece is one DÉPARTEMENT: DEPARTMENT jigsaw
fr_departement_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a boy kneeling at a low table pressing the last piece into a big wooden jigsaw puzzle map of France made of many colored pieces, his mother clapping.
fr_departement_noun.note: Un département is one of France's 101 administrative areas (le département du Rhône); each has a number used in postcodes. It also means a department of a company, store or university (le département des ventes; un département de français). A department store is un grand magasin, not un département.

fr_fichier_noun.hook: "FISHER-YAY": a FISHERman in waders casts his rod into an open drawer of the filing cabinet, hooks a FILE folder and cheers 'YAY!': FISHER-YAY
fr_fichier_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a fisherman in green waders and a bucket hat beside a tall gray filing cabinet, his fishing rod bent as he lifts a manila file folder out of an open drawer on the hook, arm raised in a cheer. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z1 into this room.
fr_fichier_noun.note: Un fichier is a file: a computer file (enregistrer un fichier) or a card index, a register of records (le fichier des clients). A paper folder is un dossier or une chemise. Ficher (no i) means to put on file or, informally, to do or to throw (Je m'en fiche = I don't care).

fr_certificat_noun.hook: "sehr-tee-fee-KAH": a proud new mom with a baby in a sling holds the BIRTH CERTIFICATE with a gold seal and a pink ribbon: BIRTH CERTIFICATE
fr_certificat_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a proud young dad with a newborn baby in a blue baby sling on his chest receiving a cream document with a round gold seal and a pink ribbon from a smiling clerk across the counter. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z1 into this room.
fr_certificat_noun.note: Un certificat is a certificate or official proof (un certificat de naissance = birth certificate; un certificat médical = doctor's note). It can also be a diploma or credential. Un certificat de scolarité proves you are enrolled at a school.

fr_decret_noun.hook: "day-KREH": a town crier in a tricorn hat unrolls a long scroll and announces the mayor's DECREE to the queue: DECREE
fr_decret_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/guichets (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a town crier in a tricorn hat and a long blue coat standing on a small step, unrolling a long blank parchment scroll and announcing with his other hand raised. Moved from the planned room R_admin_01_z1 into this room.
fr_decret_noun.note: Un décret is a decree, an order issued by the government or the President (publier un décret); un décret d'application puts a law into effect. Décréter means to decree or, loosely, to declare something by decision (Il a décrété que c'était fini).

fr_democratie_noun.hook: "day-moh-krah-SEE": a teacher points to a big poster of an ancient Greek temple with columns: Athens, the birthplace of DEMOCRACY: DEMOCRACY (Greek temple)
fr_democratie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a teacher in a cardigan pointing at a big poster of a white ancient Greek temple with columns on the left wall, two pupils looking up.
fr_democratie_noun.note: La démocratie is democracy (vivre en démocratie). Une démocratie is also a democratic country. Its opposites are la dictature (dictatorship) and la tyrannie. Un démocrate is a democrat, a supporter of democracy (not a party label in France).

fr_election_noun.hook: "ay-lehk-SYOHN": on election night a teen teller sorts paper ballots into two neat piles on a small table: the ELECTION count: ELECTION count
fr_election_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a teenage girl teller at a small table near the front sorting white paper ballots into two neat piles, a boy watching closely over her shoulder.
fr_election_noun.note: Une élection is an election (les élections municipales = local elections; se présenter aux élections = to run). Une élection can also be the choice of one person by vote (son élection à la présidence). The verb is élire; an elector is un électeur.

fr_opposition_noun.hook: "oh-poh-zee-SYOHN": on the far bench, the OPPOSITION all fold their arms and shake their heads at the proposal: OPPOSITION
fr_opposition_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): three teenagers on a bench all folding their arms and shaking their heads with frowns, facing the president's desk.
fr_opposition_noun.note: L'opposition is opposition: the parties against the government (les partis d'opposition; le chef de l'opposition) and any resistance (faire opposition à). Faire opposition à un chèque is to stop a check. Par opposition à means as opposed to.

fr_constitution_noun.hook: "kohns-tee-tew-SYOHN": two pupils solemnly carry an enormous leather-bound book, the CONSTITUTION, on a red velvet cushion: CONSTITUTION
fr_constitution_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): two pupils in white shirts carrying a huge brown leather-bound book with a gold clasp on a red velvet cushion between them.
fr_constitution_noun.note: La constitution is a country's constitution (la Constitution de 1958) and also a person's build or health (une solide constitution = a strong constitution) or how something is made up (la constitution d'une équipe = the forming of a team).

fr_presidentiel_adj.hook: "pray-zee-dahn-SYEHL": a girl climbs proudly into the tall carved PRESIDENTIAL chair at the raised desk while two classmates pull it out for her: PRESIDENTIAL chair
fr_presidentiel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a girl in a navy blazer climbing proudly into a tall carved high-backed wooden chair at the raised president's desk, two classmates pulling the chair out for her. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 into this room.
fr_presidentiel_adj.note: Présidentiel (présidentielle) means presidential (le fauteuil présidentiel; l'élection présidentielle). La présidentielle on its own is the presidential election. It also fits any chair of a club or meeting: la table présidentielle is the head table. The noun is la présidence, the presidency.

fr_parlement_noun.hook: "pahr-luh-MAHN": on the back wall a big painting of a domed PARLIAMENT building, and a girl points at it explaining where laws are made: PARLIAMENT painting
fr_parlement_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a big gilt-framed painting of a domed parliament building with columns on the back wall to the right, a girl in a ponytail pointing up at it.
fr_parlement_noun.note: Le parlement is a parliament; in France le Parlement is the Assemblée nationale plus the Sénat. Un parlementaire is a member of parliament. Before 1789 a parlement was a royal law court. Parler (to speak) is the root: a parliament is where people talk things out.

fr_vote_noun.hook: "VOT": on the right benches the members all VOTE by holding up green voting cards high: VOTE cards
fr_vote_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): four teenagers on a bench holding green voting cards high above their heads, smiling.
fr_vote_noun.note: Le vote is a vote or the voting (le vote à main levée = a show of hands; le droit de vote = the right to vote). Un vote blanc is a blank ballot. The verb is voter; a voter is un électeur, not un voteur.

fr_parti_noun.hook: "pahr-TEE (PARTY)": the members of one PARTY all wear matching orange rosettes and wave matching orange balloons, celebrating their win: PARTY
fr_parti_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): four cheering teenagers wearing matching orange rosettes, waving matching orange balloons on strings.
fr_parti_noun.note: Un parti is a political party (le parti socialiste; adhérer à un parti). Careful: a party you go to is une fête or une soirée, not un parti. Prendre parti means to take sides; un beau parti is a good match for marriage.

fr_representant_noun.hook: "ruh-pray-zahn-TAHN": classmates push a shy boy forward holding their class teddy-bear mascot: he is their REPRESENTATIVE: REPRESENTATIVE
fr_representant_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a shy boy holding a brown teddy-bear mascot being gently pushed forward by three grinning classmates.
fr_representant_noun.note: Un représentant, une représentante is a representative or delegate (les représentants du personnel), and also a sales representative (un représentant de commerce). Un représentant du peuple is an elected member of parliament.

fr_democratique_adj.hook: "day-moh-krah-TEEK": pupils each drop a bead into one of two big glass jars to choose the class pet by DEMOCRATIC vote: DEMOCRATIC jars
fr_democratique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): children taking turns dropping colored beads into one of two big glass jars on a low table, one jar with a toy bunny on its lid, one with a toy hamster.
fr_democratique_adj.note: Démocratique means democratic (un pays démocratique; une décision démocratique). The opposite is antidémocratique or autoritaire. It describes a system or decision, not a party: the U.S. Democratic Party is le Parti démocrate.

fr_gouvernemental_adj.hook: "goo-vehr-nuh-mahn-TAHL": a courier in a dark suit sets down a red leather GOVERNMENTAL dispatch box tied with a blue, white and red ribbon: GOVERNMENTAL red box
fr_gouvernemental_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a courier in a dark suit setting down a red leather dispatch box tied with a blue, white and red ribbon on the president's desk.
fr_gouvernemental_adj.note: Gouvernemental means governmental, of the government (une décision gouvernementale; une source gouvernementale). An ONG (organisation non gouvernementale) is an NGO. Le gouvernement is the government; gouverner is to govern or to steer a boat.

fr_approuver_verb.hook: "ah-proo-VAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) APPROVES loudly: he applauds and nods with a big smile at the new president: APPROVE (applause)
fr_approuver_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/parlement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, standing in the aisle applauding with big white-gloved claps and nodding with a huge smile toward the girl at the president's chair. Moved from the planned room ST_rule_seg006 into this room.
fr_approuver_verb.note: Approuver means to approve of, to agree with (J'approuve ton choix) and to approve officially, ratify (approuver un budget). Lu et approuvé = read and approved, written above a signature. The opposite is désapprouver.

fr_clairement_adv.hook: "CLAIRE-uh-MAHN": CLAIRE holds a glass of crystal-CLEAR water up to the lamp so everyone sees CLEARLY there is nothing hidden in it: CLAIRE + CLEAR
fr_clairement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a young woman with a red bob holding a glass of crystal-clear water up to the lamp light, studying it, a man beside her nodding.
fr_clairement_adv.note: Clairement means clearly: plainly visible or understandable (expliquer clairement) and obviously, without doubt (Il a clairement tort). Its opposite is vaguement or confusément. Claire is also a girl's name meaning bright, clear.

fr_franchement_adv.hook: "FRANK-uh-MAHN": a blunt man waves a hot dog, a FRANK, as he speaks FRANKLY at the microphone: no beating about the bush: FRANK-ly (a frank)
fr_franchement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a burly man in a flat cap at the standing microphone waving a hot dog in a bun in one hand, speaking bluntly with his other palm open.
fr_franchement_adv.note: Franchement means frankly, honestly (Franchement, je n'aime pas) and also really, downright (C'est franchement nul = it's downright bad). It can mean decisively, without hesitating (y aller franchement = go for it). As an exclamation, Franchement ! shows annoyance: Honestly!

fr_reellement_adv.hook: "RAY-EL-uh-MAHN": a boy pinches his own arm, wide-eyed, as the mayor hands him the microphone: is this REALLY happening?: REAL-ly (pinch)
fr_reellement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a wide-eyed boy pinching his own forearm in disbelief as a smiling woman in a tricolor scarf holds a microphone out to him.
fr_reellement_adv.note: Réellement means really, actually, genuinely (Il est réellement malade = he is genuinely ill). Réel means real; la réalité is reality. It stresses fact, not intensity: 'really big' is more often vraiment grand. Pas réellement = not really.

fr_serieusement_adv.hook: "say-ryeuh-zuh-MAHN": a lady raises her eyebrows at a man who claims his dog can speak, while the dog wears headphones: SERIOUSLY?: SERIOUSLY?
fr_serieusement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a gray-haired lady with one eyebrow raised and her hands on her hips, looking at a man proudly presenting a beagle wearing big headphones.
fr_serieusement_adv.note: Sérieusement means seriously: in earnest (travailler sérieusement) and gravely (sérieusement blessé = seriously injured). Alone, Sérieusement ? means Seriously? Are you kidding? Sérieux is serious; prendre au sérieux is to take seriously.

fr_essentiellement_adv.hook: "ay-sahn-syeh-luh-MAHN": a perfumer holds up a tiny bottle of rose ESSENCE: just one drop, ESSENTIALLY the whole rose garden: ESSENTIAL (essence)
fr_essentiellement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a woman in a lavender cardigan holding up a tiny glass bottle of pink rose essence, a single drop at its tip, a basket of red roses at her feet. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_03_z1 into this room.
fr_essentiellement_adv.note: Essentiellement means essentially, mainly, above all (Il s'agit essentiellement d'argent = it's mainly about money). L'essentiel is the main thing (C'est l'essentiel). Note l'essence is also gasoline in France, as well as an essence or extract.

fr_honnetement_adv.hook: "oh-neh-tuh-MAHN": a boy HONESTLY hands back a fat wallet he found under a chair to its delighted old owner: HONEST boy
fr_honnetement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a boy in a yellow raincoat handing a brown leather wallet back to a delighted old man with a cane. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_03_z1 into this room.
fr_honnetement_adv.note: Honnêtement means honestly, fairly (gagner sa vie honnêtement) and, at the start of a sentence, frankly (Honnêtement, je ne sais pas). It can also mean decently, reasonably well (C'est honnêtement payé). The opposite is malhonnêtement.

fr_litteralement_adv.hook: "lee-tay-rah-luh-MAHN": a man wears enormous fake ears: he is LITERALLY all ears for the debate: LITERALLY all ears
fr_litteralement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a smiling man in a sweater vest sitting forward on his chair wearing two enormous fake human ears on a headband (shaped like real human ears, skin-colored, not animal ears), one hand cupped behind an ear. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_03_z1 into this room.
fr_litteralement_adv.note: Littéralement means literally: word for word (traduire littéralement) and, informally, as an intensifier (Je suis littéralement épuisé = I'm literally exhausted). Au sens littéral = in the literal sense; the opposite is au sens figuré (figuratively).

fr_officiellement_adv.hook: "oh-fee-syeh-luh-MAHN": the debate OFFICIAL in a black blazer blows a silver whistle with his arm raised: the debate OFFICIALLY begins: OFFICIAL whistle
fr_officiellement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a stern-faced man in a black blazer blowing a silver whistle with one arm raised high, standing beside the microphone stand. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_03_z1 into this room.
fr_officiellement_adv.note: Officiellement means officially: formally, by the authorities (C'est officiellement fermé) and, sometimes, on paper as opposed to really (Officiellement, il est malade = supposedly he is ill). Officieusement means unofficially, off the record.

fr_purement_adv.hook: "pew-ruh-MAHN": a girl cradles a PURE-white dove with not one gray feather: PURELY white: PURE white dove
fr_purement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a girl in a green dress cradling a pure white dove in both hands, looking at it lovingly. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_03_z1 into this room.
fr_purement_adv.note: Purement means purely, solely (purement et simplement = purely and simply; une question purement technique). Pur means pure (l'eau pure; le pur hasard = pure chance). L'impureté is impurity.

fr_persuader_verb.hook: "pehr-swah-DAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) pleads with clasped hands and PERSUADES a grumpy old man to sign the petition: the man starts to smile and unfold his arms: PERSUADE
fr_persuader_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, pleading with clasped white-gloved hands to a grumpy old man in a gray coat who is starting to smile and unfold his arms, a clipboard and pen held out. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg014 into this room.
fr_persuader_verb.note: Persuader means to persuade or convince (persuader quelqu'un de faire quelque chose). Être persuadé que = to be convinced that. La persuasion is persuasion. The opposite is dissuader (to dissuade, talk out of).

fr_contredire_verb.hook: "CONTRA-DEER": a DEER nods yes, yes, yes, and MONSIEUR VERBE (gold beret) CONTRADICTS it, shaking his head and wagging a finger: no, no, no!: CONTRA-DEER
fr_contredire_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/debats (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a gold beret, little motion lines around his hands, shaking his head and wagging one white-gloved finger at a young deer beside him that nods eagerly. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg021 into this room.
fr_contredire_verb.note: Contredire means to contradict (contredire ses parents). It conjugates like dire except vous contredisez (not contredites). Se contredire is to contradict oneself. Une contradiction is a contradiction; l'esprit de contradiction is contrariness.

fr_refus_noun.hook: "ruh-FOOS": a grinning delivery man pushes a FOOSball table at a stern white-haired grandpa, who holds up both palms and turns his head away: REFUSAL
fr_refus_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a grinning delivery man in a brown work coat pushing a small wooden foosball table toward a stern white-haired grandfather in a gray cardigan who holds up both palms flat and turns his head away, refusing (added by crop-edit m3b_com_foos_b).
fr_refus_noun.note: Un refus is a refusal (essuyer un refus = meet with a refusal; un refus de permis = a permit denied). Ce n'est pas de refus! means I won't say no! (yes please). The verb is refuser; the opposite is une acceptation or un accord.

fr_retorquer_verb.hook: "ray-tor-KAY": a man scoffs at the plans, and MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) RETORTS at once, one finger up, snapping back a quick reply: RETORT
fr_retorquer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, turning sharply with one white-gloved finger raised and mouth open in a quick sharp reply to a scoffing man in a checked jacket who points at a model. Moved from the planned room ST_communication_seg022 into this room.
fr_retorquer_verb.note: Rétorquer means to retort, to reply sharply or quickly (rétorquer que...). It also means to turn an argument back on someone. A synonym is répliquer; une réplique is a retort or a line in a play.

fr_contrairement_adv.hook: "kohn-treh-ruh-MAHN": two brothers carry one model house and pull it in CONTRARY, opposite directions: CONTRARY
fr_contrairement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): two brothers holding the same cardboard model house between them, each pulling it toward an opposite side with determined faces.
fr_contrairement_adv.note: Contrairement à means unlike, contrary to (Contrairement à son frère, il est calme). Le contraire is the opposite (au contraire = on the contrary). Contraire is the adjective (des avis contraires = opposing views).

fr_vaguement_adv.hook: "vah-guh-MAHN": a man squints at a foggy, blurry architect's drawing and can only VAGUELY make out a house: VAGUE fog
fr_vaguement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a man in round glasses squinting hard at a large foggy, blurry drawing of a house pinned on an easel.
fr_vaguement_adv.note: Vaguement means vaguely, dimly (Je m'en souviens vaguement) or a little, slightly (vaguement inquiet = a bit worried). Careful: une vague is a wave (in the sea, or a wave of heat or of people), but vague as an adjective means vague.

fr_correctement_adv.hook: "koh-rehk-tuh-MAHN": a woman sets a spirit level on a model's roof and smiles: the bubble sits dead center, built CORRECTLY: CORRECTLY (spirit level)
fr_correctement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a woman in a blue work shirt holding a small yellow spirit level on the roof of a cardboard model house, the bubble centered, smiling.
fr_correctement_adv.note: Correctement means correctly, properly (remplir correctement un formulaire) and decently, acceptably (être payé correctement = paid reasonably). Incorrectement means incorrectly. Correct also means polite, well-behaved (Sois correct avec lui).
