fr_curieusement_adv.hook: "kew-ryeuh-zuh-MAHN": a little girl presses her nose CURIOUSLY to a tiny window of a model house to see inside: CURIOUS
fr_curieusement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a little girl with pigtails bending down to press her nose against a tiny window of a cardboard model house, eyes wide with curiosity.
fr_curieusement_adv.note: Curieusement means curiously in both senses: with curiosity (regarder curieusement) and strangely, oddly (Curieusement, personne n'est venu = oddly, nobody came). Curieux can also mean nosy. Bizarrement is a synonym for oddly.

fr_dorenavant_adv.hook: "DOH-RAY-NAH-VAN": a woman pushes a toy ice-cream VAN across the model village and sings 'DOH, RAY, NAH!': FROM NOW ON, the van comes every day: DOH-RAY-NAH-VAN
fr_dorenavant_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a cheerful woman in a striped apron singing with her mouth open, pushing a small pink-and-white toy ice-cream van along a model village street on a trestle table.
fr_dorenavant_adv.note: Dorénavant means from now on, henceforth (Dorénavant, la réunion aura lieu le lundi). It always points to the future; for 'from then on' in the past use désormais or dès lors. Synonyms: désormais, à l'avenir.

fr_definitivement_adv.hook: "day-fee-nee-tee-vuh-MAHN": a man hammers a model house firmly down onto its base: it is staying there for good, DEFINITIVELY: DEFINITIVELY
fr_definitivement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a man in a cardigan hammering a nail through the base of a cardboard model house into a trestle table with a small hammer.
fr_definitivement_adv.note: Définitivement is a false friend: it means for good, permanently (Il est parti définitivement = he left for good), not 'definitely'. For 'definitely' say certainement, sans aucun doute or vraiment. Définitif means final (une réponse définitive).

fr_neanmoins_adv.hook: "NAY-ON-MOAN": a pony loaded with rolled plans says 'NAY!' and MOANS at the weight, but NEVERTHELESS keeps on pulling: NAY-ON-MOAN
fr_neanmoins_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a small brown pony with two big rolls of blueprint plans strapped on its back, ears back, moaning, still walking forward, a girl leading it by a rope.
fr_neanmoins_adv.note: Néanmoins means nevertheless, nonetheless (C'est cher, néanmoins c'est utile). It is a little formal; in speech people say pourtant or quand même. Synonyms: cependant, toutefois.

fr_necessairement_adv.hook: "nay-say-seh-ruh-MAHN": a builder steps up to the models and NECESSARILY puts on his yellow hard hat first: no hat, no entry: NECESSARILY hard hat
fr_necessairement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a builder in an orange safety vest putting a yellow hard hat on his head with both hands.
fr_necessairement_adv.note: Nécessairement means necessarily, inevitably (Ça finira nécessairement mal). Pas nécessairement = not necessarily. It can also mean as a logical consequence. Nécessaire is necessary; le nécessaire is what is needed (faire le nécessaire = do what's needed).

fr_strictement_adv.hook: "streek-tuh-MAHN": a STRICT inspector measures a model fence's height with a yellow tape measure, frowning: STRICTLY by the rules: STRICTLY
fr_strictement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/commission (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a stern inspector in a gray suit and narrow glasses kneeling to hold a plain yellow tape measure with no numbers against a little model fence.
fr_strictement_adv.note: Strictement means strictly (strictement interdit = strictly forbidden) and, before an adjective, absolutely, utterly (strictement identique; strictement rien = nothing at all). Strict means strict or severe.
ex: Il est strictement interdit de marcher sur la pelouse.
Walking on the grass is strictly forbidden.

fr_restriction_noun.hook: "rehs-treek-SYOHN": at the climbing wall a height-RESTRICTION bar stops a tall teen: he has to duck under it, grinning: RESTRICTION bar
fr_restriction_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a tall lanky teenager ducking awkwardly under a red-and-white striped height bar at the foot of the climbing wall, a small child walking easily under it.
fr_restriction_noun.note: Une restriction is a restriction, a limit (des restrictions d'eau = water restrictions; sans restriction = without reservation). Faire des restrictions is also to express reservations. Restreindre is to restrict; restreint means limited.

fr_parite_noun.hook: "PAIR-ee-TAY": the dance club dances in PAIRS: each pair one woman and one man, exactly equal numbers: PARITY: PAIR-ITY
fr_parite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): three dancing couples, each one woman and one man, holding hands and twirling.
fr_parite_noun.note: La parité is parity, equality (la parité hommes-femmes = gender parity in elections or pay). In finance it is the parity of two currencies. Un nombre pair is an even number; parité also means evenness.

fr_sociabilite_noun.hook: "soh-syah-bee-lee-TAY": a very SOCIABLE lady pours coffee from the urn and chats merrily to a whole laughing crowd at once: SOCIABLE
fr_sociabilite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a plump cheerful lady in a flowered blouse pouring coffee from a big silver urn while chatting to four laughing people at once.
fr_sociabilite_noun.note: La sociabilité is sociability, how much someone enjoys company. Sociable means sociable, friendly; the opposite is insociable or sauvage (shy, unsociable). Les sociabilités in sociology are networks of social life.

fr_emancipation_noun.hook: "ay-mahn-see-pah-SYOHN": a girl rides off proudly on her bike while her dad holds up the training wheels he just took off: free at last: EMANCIPATION
fr_emancipation_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a girl riding off proudly on a red bicycle with arms tense and a big grin, her dad behind her holding up two small training wheels.
fr_emancipation_noun.note: L'émancipation is emancipation: freeing oneself from control (l'émancipation des femmes) and, legally, a minor gaining adult rights. S'émanciper is to become independent, to break free. Émancipé means emancipated, free-thinking.

fr_fraternite_noun.hook: "frah-tehr-nee-TAY": one brother carries his little brother piggyback across the hall: brotherhood, FRATERNITY: FRATERNITY
fr_fraternite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a teenage boy carrying his laughing little brother piggyback, both in matching blue scarves. Moved from the planned room R_society_03 into this room.
fr_fraternite_noun.note: La fraternité is brotherhood, fellowship among people; it is the third word of the French motto Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité. It is not a U.S. college fraternity (une confrérie d'étudiants). Fraternel means brotherly.

fr_citoyennete_noun.hook: "see-twah-yeh-nuh-TAY": a new citizen with her hand on her heart takes the CITIZENSHIP oath, tears of joy in her eyes, her family clapping: CITIZENSHIP
fr_citoyennete_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a woman with her hand on her heart and teary happy eyes standing tall, her husband and small son clapping behind her. Moved from the planned room R_society_03 into this room.
fr_citoyennete_noun.note: La citoyenneté is citizenship (obtenir la citoyenneté française; acquérir la nationalité is the legal term) and also active, responsible citizenship (l'éducation à la citoyenneté). Un citoyen, une citoyenne is a citizen.

fr_anonymat_noun.hook: "ah-noh-nee-MAH": a donor in a hooded coat and dark glasses slips an envelope into the club's donation box and tiptoes away, keeping his ANONYMITY: ANONYMOUS donor
fr_anonymat_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a man in a hooded gray coat and dark glasses tiptoeing away after slipping a white envelope into a wooden donation box on a club table.
fr_anonymat_noun.note: L'anonymat is anonymity (garder l'anonymat = to stay anonymous; sous couvert d'anonymat = on condition of anonymity). Anonyme means anonymous; une lettre anonyme is an anonymous letter.

fr_assentiment_noun.hook: "ah-sahn-tee-MAHN": a grandpa nods his ASSENT: yes, his grandson may join the chess club: ASSENT nod
fr_assentiment_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a smiling grandfather with a white mustache nodding at his grandson who points hopefully at a chess board on a club table.
fr_assentiment_noun.note: L'assentiment is assent, agreement, consent (donner son assentiment; d'un commun assentiment = by common consent). It is formal; in everyday speech people say l'accord or le consentement. Assentir is rare.

fr_liberalisme_noun.hook: "lee-bay-rah-LEEZM": a smiling grocer lifts the barrier of his market stall wide open: FREE trade for all, LIBERALISM: LIBERAL free trade
fr_liberalisme_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a smiling grocer in a straw hat lifting a red-and-white wooden barrier beside his little fruit stall, inviting people in with a wide sweep of his arm.
fr_liberalisme_noun.note: Le libéralisme in France usually means economic liberalism, belief in free markets and limited state control (le libéralisme économique). It is close to what Americans call free-market conservatism, not U.S. 'liberal' politics (which is de gauche or progressiste).

fr_civique_adj.hook: "see-VEEK": a teen volunteer does her CIVIC duty, sweeping up after the fair with a big broom: CIVIC duty
fr_civique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a teenage girl volunteer in a green vest sweeping the floor with a big push broom, a dustpan nearby. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_07 into this room.
fr_civique_adj.note: Civique means civic (le devoir civique = civic duty; le sens civique = public spirit). L'instruction civique is civics class. Le service civique is a French voluntary national service for young people.

fr_communal_adj.hook: "koh-mew-NAHL": the teacher from the COMMUNAL school leads a line of small pupils holding hands past the club tables: COMMUNAL school
fr_communal_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a young teacher in a red cardigan leading a short line of four small children holding hands. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_07 into this room.
fr_communal_adj.note: Communal means belonging to the commune, municipal (l'école communale = the village primary school; la salle communale = the village hall). It can mean shared, for everyone, like English 'communal', but the municipal sense is the usual one.

fr_adherer_verb.hook: "ah-day-RAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) JOINS the hiking club, and the club's big round sticker badge ADHERES so well that it stays stuck on his glove: ADHERE (sticker)
fr_adherer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/associations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, shaking his white-gloved hand to try to unstick a big round green sticker stuck on his fingertips, a hiking-club lady at a table laughing. Moved from the planned room ST_existence_seg008 into this room.
fr_adherer_verb.note: Adhérer means to join, to be a member (adhérer à un club, à un parti) and to stick, adhere (Le pneu adhère à la route). Adhérer à une idée is to support it. Un adhérent is a member; une adhésion is membership or adhesion.

fr_croyant_adj.hook: "CRAYON (krwah-YAHN)": a smiling BELIEVER with a small cross on a chain colors a drawing of the village church with a giant CRAYON: CRAYON
fr_croyant_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a smiling elderly woman with a small cross on a chain, coloring a drawing of a village church on an easel with a giant yellow crayon held in both hands.
fr_croyant_adj.note: Croyant means believing, religious (Il est très croyant = he is very religious); as a noun, un croyant, une croyante is a believer. Non croyant means non-believer. It comes from croire (to believe). Careful: crayon is French for pencil.

fr_feministe_adj.hook: "fay-mee-NEEST": a grandma in a purple, white and green suffragette sash flexes her arm like a strongwoman, and her granddaughter proudly copies her: FEMINIST
fr_feministe_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a spry grandmother wearing a purple, white and green striped sash flexing her arm like a strongwoman, her granddaughter beside her flexing too.
fr_feministe_adj.note: Féministe means feminist (un mouvement féministe); as a noun, un or une féministe. Le féminisme is feminism. The word is the same for both genders. Féminin means feminine or women's (la mode féminine).

fr_migrateur_adj.hook: "mee-grah-TUHR": a V of MIGRATORY swallows swoops in through the open skylight, heading south, and a boy points up at them: MIGRATORY swallows
fr_migrateur_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a V-shaped flock of seven swallows flying in through an open skylight panel high above, a boy below pointing up at them.
fr_migrateur_adj.note: Migrateur means migratory (les oiseaux migrateurs). As a noun, un migrateur is a migratory bird. People who migrate are des migrants; la migration is migration, of birds or people.

fr_tropical_adj.hook: "troh-pea-KAHL": in the TROPICAL corner, a man fans himself in the steamy heat beside a big potted banana palm: TROPICAL heat
fr_tropical_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a sweaty man in shirtsleeves fanning himself with his hat beside a big potted banana palm with hanging green bananas.
fr_tropical_adj.note: Tropical means tropical (un climat tropical; les forêts tropicales). It can also mean scorching, sweltering (une chaleur tropicale; une nuit tropicale = a hot night above 20°C). Les tropiques are the tropics.

fr_anthropologique_adj.hook: "ahn-troh-poh-loh-ZHEEK": an anthropologist studies an ancient clay pot through a magnifying glass, the class gathered around: ANTHROPOLOGY
fr_anthropologique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a woman scientist in a khaki vest examining an ancient clay pot through a big magnifying glass, three pupils leaning in.
fr_anthropologique_adj.note: Anthropologique means anthropological (une étude anthropologique). L'anthropologie is the study of human beings and their cultures; un anthropologue is an anthropologist. Anthropo- comes from Greek for human.

fr_aristocratique_adj.hook: "ah-rees-toh-krah-TEEK": a snooty ARISTOCRAT in a powdered wig and lace cuffs peers down his nose through a lorgnette: ARISTOCRAT
fr_aristocratique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a snooty man in a white powdered wig, a blue silk coat and lace cuffs peering down his nose through a lorgnette on a stick.
fr_aristocratique_adj.note: Aristocratique means aristocratic, of the nobility, and also refined, distinguished (des manières aristocratiques). L'aristocratie is the aristocracy; un aristocrate (informally un aristo) is an aristocrat.

fr_fonde_adj.hook: "fohn-DAY (FOUND-ed)": a man in medieval clothes lays the first stone, FOUNDING the village, a crowd in costume cheering: FOUNDED
fr_fonde_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a man in a brown medieval tunic setting a big square foundation stone into the ground with both hands, two cheering villagers in medieval costume.
fr_fonde_adj.note: Fondé means founded, established (une ville fondée au XIIe siècle) and, of an idea, well-founded, justified (une crainte fondée). Être fondé à faire = to be entitled to. Un fondé de pouvoir is a proxy or authorized agent.

fr_marxiste_adj.hook: "mahr-KSEEST": a student reads a thick red book under a marble bust of a big-bearded nineteenth-century thinker: MARXIST bust
fr_marxiste_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a student with a scarf reading a thick red book under a white marble bust of a man with a huge bushy beard on a pedestal.
fr_marxiste_adj.note: Marxiste means Marxist, following Karl Marx's ideas (une analyse marxiste); as a noun, un or une marxiste. Le marxisme is Marxism. Do not confuse with Groucho Marx's films.

fr_nomade_adj.hook: "noh-MAHD": a child peeks out of a round felt NOMAD tent, a yurt, that its family can fold up and move again and again: NOMAD yurt
fr_nomade_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a small round white felt yurt with a wooden door, a smiling child peeking out of the doorway, a girl crouching to look in.
fr_nomade_adj.note: Nomade means nomadic (un peuple nomade); as a noun, un or une nomade. It also means mobile, on the move (le travail nomade = remote, mobile work). The opposite is sédentaire (settled).

fr_residentiel_adj.hook: "ray-zee-dahn-SYEHL": a guide points at a big painting of a quiet RESIDENTIAL street of houses with gardens and swings: RESIDENTIAL street
fr_residentiel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/expo (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a young guide in a navy uniform pointing at a big framed painting on an easel of a quiet street of small houses with gardens, swings and picket fences.
fr_residentiel_adj.note: Résidentiel means residential (un quartier résidentiel = a residential area, often with a hint of upscale). Une résidence is a residence or an apartment complex; une résidence secondaire is a vacation home.

fr_corse_adj.hook: "KORS (of COURSE)": a chef carries a CORSICAN chestnut cake shaped like a mountainous island, and a guest nods: of COURSE I'll have some!: CORSICAN (of COURSE)
fr_corse_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a chef in a white jacket carrying a big brown chestnut cake shaped like a mountainous island on a platter, a guest nodding eagerly.
fr_corse_adj.note: Corse means Corsican, from Corsica (la cuisine corse); as a noun, un or une Corse is a Corsican and la Corse is the island. Le corse is the Corsican language. The word is the same in masculine and feminine.

fr_scandinave_adj.hook: "skahn-dee-NAHV": a SCANDINAVIAN guest happily assembles a flat-pack wooden chair with a little hex key: SCANDINAVIAN flat-pack
fr_scandinave_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a tall smiling blond man in a gray sweater kneeling on the floor assembling a pale wooden flat-pack chair with a small hex key, its parts around him.
fr_scandinave_adj.note: Scandinave means Scandinavian (le design scandinave); as a noun, un or une Scandinave. La Scandinavie is Scandinavia: Norway, Sweden and Denmark. Nordique (Nordic) also includes Finland and Iceland.

fr_roumain_adj.hook: "ROO-MAN": a kangaroo (a ROO) hops up to a MAN and hands him a tray of ROMANIAN stuffed cabbage rolls from its pouch: ROO-MAN
fr_roumain_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a friendly kangaroo standing upright handing a small tray of stuffed cabbage rolls to a surprised smiling man in a suit.
fr_roumain_adj.note: Roumain means Romanian (la cuisine roumaine); as a noun, un Roumain, une Roumaine; le roumain is the Romanian language and la Roumanie is Romania. Careful: romain (no u) means Roman.

fr_continental_adj.hook: "kohn-tee-nahn-TAHL": a waiter carries a CONTINENTAL breakfast tray of croissants, jam and coffee: CONTINENTAL breakfast
fr_continental_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a smiling waiter in a black vest carrying a tray with croissants, a little pot of jam, a coffee cup and orange juice.
fr_continental_adj.note: Continental means continental, of a continent (le climat continental = hot summers and cold winters). In France, la France continentale is mainland France, as opposed to Corsica and the overseas territories. Le petit-déjeuner continental is a continental breakfast.

fr_multinational_adj.hook: "mewl-tee-nah-syoh-NAHL": a busy MULTINATIONAL businesswoman wears five wristwatches up her arm, each set to a different country: MULTINATIONAL watches
fr_multinational_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a businesswoman in a gray suit proudly holding up her forearm wearing five wristwatches with plain faces, phone in her other hand.
fr_multinational_adj.note: Multinational means multinational (une entreprise multinationale); une multinationale is a multinational company. Multi- means many: multiculturel, multilingue.

fr_metropolitain_adj.hook: "may-troh-poh-lee-TAN": a toy METRO train runs around the table on a little track, and a boy watches it go: METRO train
fr_metropolitain_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a little blue toy subway train running on a small track around a centerpiece on the table, a boy with his chin on his hands watching it.
fr_metropolitain_adj.note: Métropolitain means metropolitan; in France it usually means mainland France (la France métropolitaine, as opposed to the overseas départements). Le métropolitain is the full name of the Paris subway, now le métro. Une métropole is a big city.

fr_constituant_adj.hook: "kohns-tee-TWAHN": a girl lays out the CONSTITUENT parts of a sandwich side by side: bread, cheese, tomato and lettuce: CONSTITUENT parts
fr_constituant_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a girl at the table arranging bread slices, a slice of cheese, tomato slices and a lettuce leaf neatly side by side on a white plate.
fr_constituant_adj.note: Constituant means constituent, making up a whole (les éléments constituants). L'Assemblée constituante was the body that wrote a constitution in 1789 and after. As a noun, un constituant is a component.

fr_territorial_adj.hook: "teh-ree-toh-RYAHL": a TERRITORIAL goose spreads its wings and hisses at a guest who steps onto its patch of floor: TERRITORIAL goose
fr_territorial_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a white goose spreading its wings and hissing at a startled guest stepping back with a plate in hand.
fr_territorial_adj.note: Territorial means territorial (les eaux territoriales; un animal territorial). In France, la fonction publique territoriale is local government service, and une collectivité territoriale is a local authority (region, département, commune).

fr_suisse_adj.hook: "SWEES": guests dip bread into a bubbling pot of SWISS cheese fondue on long forks: SWISS fondue
fr_suisse_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): three guests dipping cubes of bread on long forks into a bubbling pot of melted cheese fondue on a small burner. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_05 into this room.
fr_suisse_adj.note: Suisse means Swiss (le chocolat suisse); as a noun, un Suisse, une Suissesse or une Suisse; la Suisse is Switzerland. In France, un petit-suisse is a small fresh cheese for children. Manger en suisse means to eat alone without sharing.

fr_quebecois_adj.hook: "kay-bay-KWAH": a guest from QUEBEC pours golden maple syrup over a stack of pancakes, a red maple-leaf pin on her sweater: QUEBEC maple syrup
fr_quebecois_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/nations (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE3 build): a smiling woman in a red plaid shirt with a red maple-leaf pin pouring golden maple syrup from a jug over a stack of pancakes. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_05 into this room.
fr_quebecois_adj.note: Québécois means from Quebec (la culture québécoise); as a noun, un Québécois, une Québécoise. Le québécois is also the French spoken in Quebec. The province is le Québec, the city is Québec (no article).

fr_identification_noun.hook: "ee-dahn-tee-fee-kah-SYOHN": a clerk at a side desk holds up a man's ID card and checks the photo on it: IDENTIFICATION: IDENTIFICATION
fr_identification_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a woman clerk in a gray jacket at a small wooden side desk holding up an ID card with a man's photo, checking it.
fr_identification_noun.note: Cognate of English identification. L'identification is identifying someone or something (l'identification d'un suspect; une pièce d'identification). It also means identifying with someone, as with a character in a film (l'identification au héros). The verb is identifier; s'identifier à means to identify with.

fr_soumission_noun.hook: "soo-mee-SYOHN": a weary traveler kneels and waves a white handkerchief at a stern clerk with folded arms: he gives in, total SUBMISSION: SUBMISSION
fr_soumission_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a weary bearded traveler kneeling on the checkered floor beside his suitcase, holding out a white handkerchief at shoulder height and waving it in surrender toward a stern woman clerk with folded arms.
fr_soumission_noun.note: Cognate of English submission. La soumission is submission, giving in to someone's power (la soumission à l'autorité); its opposite is la révolte or la résistance. In business it is also a tender or bid (une soumission pour un marché public). To submit a form is usually déposer or remettre, not soumettre.

fr_britannique_adj.hook: "bree-tah-NEEK": a young woman sits on a suitcase covered with a big Union Jack sticker: BRITISH: BRITISH
fr_britannique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a young woman with a ponytail sitting on top of her own navy suitcase, which has one big Union Jack flag sticker on its side, holding her passport. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_britannique_adj.note: Cognate of English British. Britannique means British (un passeport britannique; les îles Britanniques = the British Isles). Un Britannique, une Britannique is a British person, with a capital letter. English alone is anglais, and Breton (from Brittany, in France) is breton: a different place.

fr_titulaire_adj.hook: "tee-tew-LEHR": a proud man wears a gold championship TITLE belt and holds up his own passport: he is its TITLE-HOLDER: TITLE-holder
fr_titulaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a proud stocky man with a gold championship belt over his shoulder holding up a passport in his raised hand, grinning. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_titulaire_adj.note: Cognate of English titular. Titulaire means holding a post or document in your own name: le titulaire du passeport (the passport holder), un professeur titulaire (a tenured teacher), un joueur titulaire (a first-team player, not a substitute). Its opposite is remplaçant or suppléant (a substitute) and, for teachers, contractuel.

fr_diplomatique_adj.hook: "dee-ploh-mah-TEEK": two diplomats in dark suits shake hands at the counter: DIPLOMATIC talks: DIPLOMATIC
fr_diplomatique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): two diplomats in dark suits, a woman and a man, shaking hands in front of the counter. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_diplomatique_adj.note: Cognate of English diplomatic. Diplomatique means diplomatic, about relations between countries (un passeport diplomatique, la valise diplomatique = the diplomatic bag) and, of a person, tactful (une réponse diplomatique). Its opposite in the second sense is maladroit or brutal (tactless).

fr_permanent_adj.hook: "pehr-mah-NAHN": a stonemason chisels a blank stone tablet leaning on the wall: carved in stone, it is PERMANENT: PERMANENT, set in stone
fr_permanent_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a stonemason in a white cap and leather apron kneeling and tapping a chisel with a mallet on a big blank gray stone tablet leaning against the wall. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_permanent_adj.note: Cognate of English permanent. Permanent means permanent, lasting (un titre de séjour permanent; un contrat permanent) or constant (un danger permanent). Its opposite is temporaire or provisoire. Une permanence is a duty office or open hours (la permanence du député); une permanente is a perm in hair.

fr_australien_adj.hook: "ohs-trah-LYAN": a young backpacker in a bush hat holds a wooden boomerang while he waits his turn: AUSTRALIAN: AUSTRALIAN
fr_australien_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a young backpacker in shorts and a wide-brimmed bush hat with a backpack, holding a big wooden boomerang in one hand and his papers in the other. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_05 into this room.
fr_australien_adj.note: Cognate of English Australian. Australien means Australian (un passeport australien); fem. australienne. Un Australien, une Australienne is an Australian person, with a capital letter. Don't mix it up with autrichien (Austrian).

fr_obligatoirement_adv.hook: "oh-blee-gah-twah-ruh-MAHN": a security guard points sternly at yellow footprints painted on the floor where everyone OBLIGATORILY has to stand: OBLIGATORY
fr_obligatoirement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a security guard in a navy uniform pointing sternly down at a pair of yellow footprints painted on the checkered floor, where a confused old man must step. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_04 into this room.
fr_obligatoirement_adv.note: Cognate of English obligatorily. Obligatoirement means necessarily, compulsorily: Il faut obligatoirement un passeport (a passport is required). In speech it also means inevitably (Ça devait obligatoirement arriver = it was bound to happen). Its opposite is facultativement (optionally); pas obligatoirement means not necessarily.

fr_envoye_noun.hook: "ahn-vwah-YAY": an ENVOY in a long dark coat with a blue sash hands a sealed letter with a red wax seal to an official: ENVOY
fr_envoye_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an envoy in a long dark coat with a blue sash handing a cream letter with a red wax seal to a gray-haired official. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_envoye_noun.note: Cognate of English envoy. Un envoyé, une envoyée is an envoy, someone sent on a mission (un envoyé spécial = a special envoy, also a reporter sent abroad). It is the past participle of envoyer (to send). Un envoi is a parcel or a sending.

fr_consulat_noun.hook: "kohn-sew-LAH": behind his own glass window, with a small foreign flag on his desk, a consul runs the CONSULATE counter: CONSULATE
fr_consulat_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a consul in a dark suit seated behind a glass service window with a small green-and-yellow foreign flag on his desk.
fr_consulat_noun.note: Cognate of English consulate. Un consulat is a consulate, the office of a consul in a foreign city (le consulat de France à New York). Un consul runs it; une ambassade (embassy) is in the capital. Historically, le Consulat was France's government of 1799-1804, under Napoleon.

fr_visa_noun.hook: "vee-ZAH": at the counter a woman in a red coat holds up a big colorful stamped VISA page: VISA
fr_visa_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a woman in a red coat at the counter holding up a big colorful stamped visa page.
fr_visa_noun.note: Cognate of English visa. Un visa is a visa (un visa de tourisme; une demande de visa). It also means an official stamp of approval (le visa de censure for a film). The bank card brand is Visa too. Its opposite is un refus de visa (a visa refusal).

fr_formulaire_noun.hook: "for-mew-LEHR": an old man kneels on the floor filling in a FORM so long that it coils across the floor in big loops: FORM-ULAIRE
fr_formulaire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an old man in a tweed jacket kneeling on the checkered floor and writing with a pen on one blank white paper form so long that it lies in big folded loops across the floor.
fr_formulaire_noun.note: Un formulaire is a form to fill in (remplir un formulaire; un formulaire en ligne = an online form). Don't confuse it with une forme (a shape) or une formule (a formula or a set menu). Un formulaire vierge is a blank form.

fr_laissez_passer_noun.hook: "LAY-say-PASS": a guard lifts the red-and-white barrier arm and LETS a young man PASS when he shows a small pass card: LET-PASS
fr_laissez_passer_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/visas (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): inside this room, at the right end of the counter: a guard in a navy cap lifting a red-and-white striped barrier arm, a young man with a messenger bag walking through and holding up a small blank pass card.
fr_laissez_passer_noun.note: Un laissez-passer is a pass or permit that lets you through (un laissez-passer de presse; an emergency travel document for someone who lost a passport). Its plural is unchanged (des laissez-passer). Laisser passer, as a verb, means to let through; ne pas laisser passer means to refuse to let through.

fr_republique_noun.hook: "ray-pew-BLEEK": an aide polishes a white plaster bust of MARIANNE in her soft cap, the symbol of the French REPUBLIC: MARIANNE of the REPUBLIC
fr_republique_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a young woman aide kneeling on the carpet and polishing with a cloth a white plaster bust of Marianne, a young woman wearing a soft Phrygian cap, on a low white pedestal. Moved from the planned room R_politics_01 into this room.
fr_republique_noun.note: Cognate of English republic. Une république is a republic, a state with an elected head and no king (la République française; la Ve République since 1958). Its opposite is une monarchie. In speech, en pleine république means in a free country; Marianne is its symbol in every town hall.

fr_municipalite_noun.hook: "mew-nee-see-pah-lee-TAY": a councilwoman traces with her finger the red boundary line around the whole village on a big framed aerial map: the MUNICIPALITY: MUNICIPALITY
fr_municipalite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a councilwoman in a green jacket tracing with her finger a red line drawn around a village on a big framed aerial map hanging on the paneling. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_municipalite_noun.note: Cognate of English municipality. La municipalité is the municipality, a town as a local government, and also its elected council and mayor (la municipalité a décidé... = the town council decided). The adjective is municipal. Une commune is the basic French local unit.

fr_confidentiel_adj.hook: "kohn-fee-dahn-SYEHL": a secretary presses a big red seal onto a folder and holds a finger to her lips: CONFIDENTIAL: CONFIDENTIAL
fr_confidentiel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a secretary with glasses at the corner of the big desk pressing a big red wax seal onto a manila folder, her other finger on her lips. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_confidentiel_adj.note: Cognate of English confidential. Confidentiel means confidential, secret (un document confidentiel; à titre confidentiel = in confidence). It can also mean little known, for a small audience (un film confidentiel = a niche film). Its opposite is public.

fr_explicitement_adv.hook: "ehk-splee-see-tuh-MAHN": an aide points step by step at a big clear picture diagram on an easel (a house, an arrow, a key) and spells it all out EXPLICITLY: EXPLICITLY
fr_explicitement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an aide pointing with a pointer at a big easel board showing a simple clear picture diagram of a house, an arrow and a key, two listeners nodding. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_04 into this room.
fr_explicitement_adv.note: Cognate of English explicitly. Explicitement means explicitly, clearly and in so many words (Il l'a dit explicitement). Its opposite is implicitement (implicitly, without saying it). The adjective explicite also describes adult content (des paroles explicites).

fr_executif_adj.hook: "ehg-zay-kew-TEEF": the boss sits in a big high-backed leather EXECUTIVE chair at the carved desk and signs a document with a fountain pen: EXECUTIVE
fr_executif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a gray-haired woman in a dark suit sitting in a big high-backed brown leather executive chair at the carved walnut desk, signing a document with a fountain pen. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_executif_adj.note: Cognate of English executive. Exécutif means executive, carrying out decisions: le pouvoir exécutif (the executive power: president and government), as opposed to législatif (making laws) and judiciaire (courts). L'exécutif is also a noun for the government. A business executive is un cadre.

fr_discret_adj.hook: "dees-KREH": a hunched young aide creeps DISCREETLY behind the boss's chair with her coffee, careful not to make a sound: DISCREET
fr_discret_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a young aide in a dark suit creeping quietly behind the executive chair, bent forward with hunched shoulders and a careful sideways glance, carrying a small tray with a coffee cup. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_discret_adj.note: Cognate of English discreet. Discret means discreet, keeping quiet about things (Sois discret !), and also modest, unobtrusive (une couleur discrète, un maquillage discret). Fem. discrète. Its opposite is indiscret (nosy, tactless) or voyant (flashy). In math it means discrete.

fr_interne_adj.hook: "an-TEHRN": a young INTERN pushes a cart of INTERNAL mail from office to office inside the building: INTERNAL INTERN
fr_interne_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a young intern in a lanyard and sneakers pushing a small wooden mail cart piled with envelopes along the green carpet. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_interne_adj.note: Cognate of English internal. Interne means internal, inside (le courrier interne = internal mail; une hémorragie interne). Its opposite is externe. Un interne, une interne is a hospital resident doctor or a boarder at school, not an office intern (that is un stagiaire).

fr_ministeriel_adj.hook: "mee-nees-tay-RYEHL": a visiting government minister in a dark suit with a tiny tricolor lapel pin hugs his fat red leather MINISTERIAL portfolio: MINISTERIAL
fr_ministeriel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a visiting minister with glasses in a dark suit with a tiny round tricolor lapel pin, hugging a fat red leather portfolio case to his chest. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_ministeriel_adj.note: Cognate of English ministerial. Ministériel means ministerial, of a government minister (un remaniement ministériel = a cabinet reshuffle; un arrêté ministériel = a ministerial order). Un ministre is a minister; le ministère is the ministry. It is not about church ministers.

fr_categoriquement_adv.hook: "kah-tay-goh-ree-kuh-MAHN": an old farmer folds his arms and turns his head away with a stern frown from a saleswoman offering a giant novelty pen: no, CATEGORICALLY no!: CATEGORICALLY no
fr_categoriquement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an old farmer in a flat cap with folded arms and a stern frown turning away from a smiling saleswoman in a gray suit holding out a giant novelty pen as long as her arm. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_04 into this room.
fr_categoriquement_adv.note: Cognate of English categorically. Catégoriquement means categorically, flatly (refuser catégoriquement; nier catégoriquement = to flatly deny). It is used most with refusals and denials. A softer opposite is avec hésitation or à demi (halfheartedly).

fr_gouverneur_noun.hook: "goo-vehr-NUHR": a portly bank GOVERNOR in a pinstripe suit sits on a footstool and proudly holds up a fresh uncut sheet of new banknotes (blank play notes in the picture): GOVERNOR
fr_gouverneur_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a portly gray-haired bank governor in a pinstripe suit and a gold watch chain, sitting on a low wooden footstool, proudly holding up a big uncut sheet of pale green paper printed as a grid of blank play banknotes, with no faces, numbers, symbols or real money.
fr_gouverneur_noun.note: Cognate of English governor. Un gouverneur is a governor: of a central bank (le gouverneur de la Banque de France), a colony or a US state. It comes from Latin gubernator, a ship's steersman. A school or prison governor is un directeur.

fr_gouvernement_noun.hook: "goo-vehr-nuh-MAHN": on the paneling hangs a big framed painting of the GOVERNMENT: ministers sitting around one long table with the president: GOVERNMENT
fr_gouvernement_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a big gilt-framed painting on the walnut paneling showing a group of ministers in suits sitting around one long table. Moved from the planned room R_politics_01 into this room.
fr_gouvernement_noun.note: Cognate of English government. Le gouvernement is the government: the prime minister and ministers (le gouvernement a démissionné = the cabinet resigned). It also means the act of governing. In France it is distinct from l'État (the state) and from l'administration (civil servants).

fr_confident_noun.hook: "kohn-fee-DAHN": an old man whispers a secret into the ear of his best friend, his CONFIDANT, who listens with a hand cupped to his ear: CONFIDANT
fr_confident_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/cabinet (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an old man in a gray suit leaning to whisper into the ear of his best friend, a smiling old man with a hand cupped behind his ear. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_confident_noun.note: Cognate of English confidant. Un confident, une confidente is a confidant, someone you tell your secrets to (Elle est ma confidente). False friend: confident (sure of yourself) is sûr de soi or confiant. Une confidence is a secret you share (faire une confidence).

fr_declaration_noun.hook: "day-klah-rah-SYOHN": a spokeswoman at the podium reads out an official DECLARATION from a sheet of paper: DECLARATION
fr_declaration_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a spokeswoman in a teal suit standing at the small wooden podium on the low stage reading aloud from a blank sheet of paper. Moved from the planned room R_politics_03 into this room.
fr_declaration_noun.note: Cognate of English declaration. Une déclaration is a statement or declaration (faire une déclaration à la presse; la Déclaration des droits de l'homme). It is also a form you file (la déclaration d'impôts = tax return) and a declaration of love (une déclaration d'amour). Its opposite is un démenti (a denial).

fr_mediatique_adj.hook: "may-dyah-TEEK": a forest of MEDIA microphones on stands and a big TV camera crowd toward the podium: MEDIA
fr_mediatique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a dense cluster of many microphones in different colors on stands crowding in front of the podium, a TV cameraman with a big shoulder camera filming. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_06 into this room.
fr_mediatique_adj.note: Cognate of English media. Médiatique means about the media (la couverture médiatique = media coverage; un événement médiatique). Said of a person, it means media-savvy or much in the media (un ministre très médiatique). Its rough opposite is discret or méconnu (low-profile). Les médias are the media.

fr_techniquement_adv.hook: "tehk-nee-kuh-MAHN": a TECHNICIAN on her knees untangles a huge knot of cables behind the TV camera: TECHNICALLY
fr_techniquement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a technician in a black T-shirt and headphones kneeling on the floor untangling a huge knot of black cables. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_techniquement_adv.note: Cognate of English technically. Techniquement means technically: in technical terms (techniquement parfait) and also strictly speaking, in theory (Techniquement, c'est interdit, mais...). Its opposite in the second sense is en pratique (in practice).

fr_anonyme_adj.hook: "ah-noh-NEEM": a man in a trench coat, hat and dark glasses hides his face behind a blank newspaper in the back row: ANONYMOUS: ANONYMOUS
fr_anonyme_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a man in a beige trench coat, a hat and dark glasses sitting in a folding chair hiding his face behind a wide-open blank newspaper. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_anonyme_adj.note: Cognate of English anonymous. Anonyme means anonymous, unnamed (une lettre anonyme; un don anonyme). It also means faceless, impersonal (un immeuble anonyme). Une société anonyme (SA) is a public limited company. Its opposite is signé or connu.

fr_paradoxalement_adv.hook: "pah-rah-dok-sah-luh-MAHN": a man SHUSHES the noisy room through a giant megaphone, PARADOXICALLY making the most noise of all: PARADOXICALLY
fr_paradoxalement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a man in a sweater vest standing on a chair shushing the room through a giant red megaphone.
fr_paradoxalement_adv.note: Cognate of English paradoxically. Paradoxalement means paradoxically, against what you would expect (Paradoxalement, il travaille mieux fatigué). It is often used to introduce a surprising fact. The adjective is paradoxal; un paradoxe is a paradox.

fr_inedit_adj.hook: "ee-nay-DEE": a reporter whips a cloth off an easel to reveal a never-before-seen UN-EDITED photo, and the room gasps: UN-EDITED
fr_inedit_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a reporter pulling a cloth off a big framed picture of a mountain on an easel, a woman beside it gasping. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_inedit_adj.note: Inédit means never seen or published before (des photos inédites; un texte inédit) and, by extension, new, unprecedented (une situation inédite). False friend: it does not mean unedited (that is non retouché or brut). Its opposite is déjà vu or connu.

fr_vraisemblablement_adv.hook: "VRAY SAHM-blab-luh-MAHN": a reporter-detective with a magnifying glass follows muddy paw prints to a puppy with a muddy nose: it SEEMS TRUE, PROBABLY the puppy did it: PROBABLY, VRAI SEMBLE
fr_vraisemblablement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a reporter in a checked cap bending with a big magnifying glass over a trail of muddy paw prints leading to a guilty-looking puppy with a muddy nose. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_vraisemblablement_adv.note: Vraisemblablement means probably, very likely (Il viendra vraisemblablement demain). It comes from vrai (true) and semblable (seeming): seemingly true. Its opposite is invraisemblablement or peu probablement. The adjective vraisemblable means plausible, likely.

fr_publicitaire_adj.hook: "pew-blee-see-TEHR": an ad man unrolls a big colorful ADVERTISING poster of a smiling toothpaste tube for the cameras: PUBLICITY POSTER
fr_publicitaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an ad man in a bright yellow jacket unrolling a big colorful poster showing a cartoon smiling toothpaste tube. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_06 into this room.
fr_publicitaire_adj.note: Cognate of English publicity, but it means advertising. Publicitaire means about advertising (une affiche publicitaire = an advertising poster; un spot publicitaire = a commercial). Un publicitaire, une publicitaire is an advertising executive. Not publicity in the sense of fame, which is la notoriété; la publicité (la pub) is advertising.

fr_ironiquement_adv.hook: "ee-roh-nee-kuh-MAHN": a TV weatherman proudly holds up a sunny forecast picture while water IRONICALLY drips on his head from a leak in the ceiling: IRONICALLY
fr_ironiquement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a TV weatherman in a bow tie proudly holding up a board with a bright yellow sun picture while water drips from a ceiling leak onto his head and soaks his hair. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_ironiquement_adv.note: Cognate of English ironically. Ironiquement means ironically: with irony, saying the opposite of what you mean (répondre ironiquement), and by an irony of fate (Ironiquement, il pleuvait le jour de la fête du soleil). The adjective is ironique.

fr_faussement_adv.hook: "FOSS-MAHN": a young reporter in joke nose-and-mustache glasses grins FALSELY innocent: FALSELY
fr_faussement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a young reporter in a black sweater on a folding chair wearing joke glasses with a big pink plastic nose and a bushy mustache, grinning with a falsely innocent look. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_faussement_adv.note: Faussement means falsely, wrongly (accusé faussement) or with pretense (faussement modeste = falsely modest; d'un air faussement innocent). Its opposite is vraiment or sincèrement. The adjective is faux, fausse (false, fake).

fr_positivement_adv.hook: "poh-zee-tee-vuh-MAHN": a cheerful woman in the front row gives two big thumbs up, reacting POSITIVELY: POSITIVELY
fr_positivement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a cheerful older woman in a front-row folding chair giving two big thumbs up, beaming. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_positivement_adv.note: Cognate of English positively. Positivement means positively, in a good way (réagir positivement) or in a definite way (C'est positivement faux = it's flat-out wrong). Its opposite is négativement. The adjective positif also means a positive test result.

fr_format_noun.hook: "for-MAH": a kneeling photographer compares two empty picture frames, a tall one and a wide one, choosing the photo FORMAT: FORMAT
fr_format_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/presse (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a photographer with a camera around his neck kneeling on the floor and comparing two empty picture frames, one tall and narrow and one wider. Moved from the planned room R_admin_02 into this room.
fr_format_noun.note: Cognate of English format. Le format is a format or size (le format A4; un format de poche = pocket-size; le format paysage = landscape format). It is also a computer file format (au format PDF). Formater means to format a disk, and figuratively to mold someone's mind.

fr_unanimite_noun.hook: "ew-nah-nee-mee-TAY": three councilors at a table all raise their right hands at exactly the same moment: UNANIMITY: UNANIMITY
fr_unanimite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): three councilors at a table, a woman in purple, a woman with a ponytail and a man in a navy jacket, all raising their right hands high at the same moment, smiling.
fr_unanimite_noun.note: Cognate of English unanimity. L'unanimité is unanimity, everyone agreeing (voter à l'unanimité = to vote unanimously; faire l'unanimité = to win everyone over). Its opposite is la division or le désaccord; à la majorité means by a majority, not by everyone.

fr_categorie_noun.hook: "kah-tay-goh-REE": a clerk sorts envelopes into three wire baskets, each one a different CATEGORY: CATEGORY
fr_categorie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a woman clerk in a cardigan standing at the end of the left trestle table sorting envelopes into three wire baskets, a white one, a yellow one and a blue one. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_categorie_noun.note: Cognate of English category. Une catégorie is a category or class (une catégorie d'âge; un hôtel de première catégorie = a first-class hotel). Catégoriel means sectional, for one group (des revendications catégorielles). Catégorique (categorical, flat) is a different word: un refus catégorique.

fr_procuration_noun.hook: "proh-kew-rah-SYOHN": a woman with her leg in a big plaster cast, stuck at home for her CURE, holds up the PROXY form she has just signed so a friend can act FOR (PRO) her and vote in her place: PRO-CURE-ACTION: PRO-CURE-ACTION
fr_procuration_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a woman with her leg in a big white plaster cast sitting on a chair with crutches, holding up a signed sheet of paper in one hand. Moved from the planned room R_admin_02 into this room.
fr_procuration_noun.note: Une procuration is a proxy, a written authorization to act for someone (voter par procuration = to vote by proxy; donner procuration à quelqu'un). In banking it is a power of attorney over an account. The person who receives it is le mandataire. Its opposite is acting in person, en personne.

fr_primaire_adj.hook: "pree-MEHR": a little girl sits on the floor and paints with only the three PRIMARY colors, red, yellow and blue: PRIMARY
fr_primaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a little girl sitting cross-legged on the floor painting on a big sheet with three paint pots, one red, one yellow and one blue. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_primaire_adj.note: Cognate of English primary. Primaire means primary, first in order (les couleurs primaires; une élection primaire; l'école primaire = elementary school, for ages 6 to 11). Said of a person or idea, it is negative: simplistic, crude (un raisonnement primaire). Its opposite is secondaire.

fr_electoral_adj.hook: "ay-lehk-toh-RAHL": two volunteers tip the big clear ELECTORAL ballot box upside down and a heap of envelopes pours onto the table: ELECTORAL
fr_electoral_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): two volunteers, a man and a woman, lifting the big clear plastic ballot box and tipping it upside down so a heap of envelopes pours out onto the middle trestle table.
fr_electoral_adj.note: Cognate of English electoral. Électoral means about elections (une campagne électorale; la liste électorale = the voter roll; un bureau électoral). Fem. électorale, plural électoraux. L'électorat is the electorate, and un électeur, une électrice is a voter.

fr_deuxiemement_adv.hook: "deuh-zyeh-muh-MAHN": a teller in a bow tie holds up TWO fingers, DEUX, as he reads out his second point: secondly: DEUX (two)
fr_deuxiemement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a gray-haired teller in a bow tie standing behind the middle table, holding up two fingers high in a V and talking. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_deuxiemement_adv.note: Deuxièmement means secondly, in the second place, when listing points (Premièrement…, deuxièmement…). It is built on deuxième (second) from deux (two). Its partners are premièrement (firstly) and troisièmement (thirdly); in speech people often say ensuite or en second lieu instead.

fr_politiquement_adv.hook: "poh-lee-tee-kuh-MAHN": two men in red and blue ties talk POLITICALLY, each wagging a finger to make his point: POLITICALLY
fr_politiquement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): two middle-aged men, one in a flat cap and a red tie and one in a blue tie, standing face to face and talking politics, each raising a pointing finger. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_politiquement_adv.note: Cognate of English politically. Politiquement means politically, from the point of view of politics (politiquement engagé = politically active; politiquement correct). Its opposite is apolitiquement, rarely used; people say sans parti pris (without taking sides) instead.

fr_respectivement_adv.hook: "rehs-pehk-tee-vuh-MAHN": twin boys in a red shirt and a blue shirt hold a red balloon and a blue balloon, RESPECTIVELY: RESPECTIVELY
fr_respectivement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): twin boys standing side by side, one in a red shirt holding a red balloon and one in a blue shirt holding a blue balloon. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_respectivement_adv.note: Cognate of English respectively. Respectivement means respectively, each in the order given (Ils ont respectivement 8 et 10 ans = They are 8 and 10, respectively). It has nothing to do with respect; for respectfully say respectueusement.

fr_equivalent_noun.hook: "ay-kee-vah-LAHN": a volunteer sets two piles of envelopes on an old balance and the pans hang perfectly level: each pile is the EQUIVALENT of the other: EQUIVALENT
fr_equivalent_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a young woman volunteer with glasses beside an old brass balance scale holding two equal piles of envelopes, its two pans hanging perfectly level. Moved from the planned room R_society_03 into this room.
fr_equivalent_noun.note: Cognate of English equivalent. Un équivalent is an equivalent, something of equal value or meaning (Il n'y a pas d'équivalent en anglais). It is also an adjective: équivalent à (equal to). Its opposite is une différence or un écart. The verb is équivaloir à, to amount to.

fr_citoyen_noun.hook: "see-twah-YAN": a proud boy holds his brand-new voter card high above his head: a CITIZEN voting for the first time: CITIZEN
fr_citoyen_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a proud teenage boy in a striped sweater holding one small blank card high above his head with both hands, beaming. Moved from the planned room R_politics_02 into this room.
fr_citoyen_noun.note: Cognate of English citizen. Un citoyen, une citoyenne is a citizen, a member of the nation with rights and duties (un citoyen français; le devoir du citoyen). As an adjective it means civic-minded (un geste citoyen). La citoyenneté is citizenship. The opposite is un étranger, a foreigner.

fr_concitoyen_noun.hook: "kohn-see-twah-YAN": two neighbors from the same village shake hands warmly: FELLOW CITIZENS: FELLOW CITIZEN
fr_concitoyen_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/electoral (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): two neighbors, a stout woman in a headscarf and a tall man in overalls, shaking hands warmly and smiling. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_concitoyen_noun.note: Cognate of English citizen, with con- meaning with: un concitoyen, une concitoyenne is a fellow citizen, someone from the same town or country (Mes chers concitoyens = My fellow citizens, a classic opening of a mayor's speech). Its opposite is un étranger, an outsider.

fr_dictature_noun.hook: "deek-tah-TEWR": a little boy in a paper general's hat plays DICTATOR, arms crossed, barking orders at the whole class: a DICTATORSHIP: DICTATORSHIP
fr_dictature_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a little boy in a folded paper general's hat with a feather, arms crossed, scowling as he barks orders at the class. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 into this room.
fr_dictature_noun.note: Cognate of English dictatorship (via dictator). Une dictature is a dictatorship, rule by one person or group with no free elections (vivre sous une dictature; la dictature militaire). Figuratively it means any tyranny (la dictature de la mode). Its opposite is la démocratie. The ruler is un dictateur.

fr_legislation_noun.hook: "lay-zhee-slah-SYOHN": a teacher piles yet another thick law book onto a wobbling tower of LEGISLATION: LEGISLATION
fr_legislation_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a woman teacher in a green cardigan placing one more thick red law book onto a tall stack of thick red law books on a desk. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_legislation_noun.note: Cognate of English legislation. La législation is legislation, the body of laws on a subject (la législation du travail = labor law; la législation en vigueur = the laws in force). It is a collective noun: one single law is une loi. To legislate is légiférer.

fr_charte_noun.hook: "SHAHRT": a girl unrolls a long parchment CHARTER with a red wax seal at the bottom: CHARTER
fr_charte_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a girl unrolling a long blank parchment scroll with a big red wax seal at its bottom end, holding it open with both arms. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_charte_noun.note: Cognate of English charter. Une charte is a charter, a founding text of rights or rules (la Charte des Nations unies; la charte de l'environnement; une charte de qualité = a code of practice). It is not a chart: a chart is un graphique or, at sea, une carte marine.

fr_constitutionnel_adj.hook: "kohns-tee-tew-syoh-NEHL": a proud librarian holds up the big bound book of the CONSTITUTION with both hands: CONSTITUTIONAL
fr_constitutionnel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a gray-haired librarian standing in the middle of the room, proudly holding up with both hands a big thick blank book bound in blue, white and red.
fr_constitutionnel_adj.note: Cognate of English constitutional. Constitutionnel means constitutional, in line with the constitution (le Conseil constitutionnel; une loi constitutionnelle). Fem. constitutionnelle. Its opposite is anticonstitutionnel, unconstitutional. Said of a person's health it means constitutional too (une faiblesse constitutionnelle = an inborn weakness).

fr_legislatif_adj.hook: "lay-zhee-slah-TEEF": a girl at a small lectern reads out a brand-new law to the class: LEGISLATIVE work: LEGISLATIVE
fr_legislatif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a girl in a navy blazer standing at a small wooden lectern, reading aloud from a blank sheet of paper with a serious face.
fr_legislatif_adj.note: Cognate of English legislative. Législatif means legislative, about making laws (le pouvoir législatif = the legislature; les élections législatives = the parliamentary elections). Fem. législative. It goes with l'exécutif and le judiciaire, the three powers.

fr_federal_adj.hook: "fay-day-RAHL": a finished jigsaw map lies on the floor, its separate colored regions joined into one FEDERAL country: FEDERAL
fr_federal_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a big finished jigsaw puzzle map lying on the floor, made of differently colored regions that together form one country. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_federal_adj.note: Cognate of English federal. Fédéral means federal, made of states united under a central government (l'État fédéral; la Suisse est un pays fédéral). Plural fédéraux. Its opposite is unitaire (a unitary state, like France) or centralisé. La fédération also means a sports federation.

fr_parlementaire_adj.hook: "pahr-luh-mahn-TEHR": a boy sets tiny figures in the red seats of a half-circle model PARLIAMENT: PARLIAMENTARY
fr_parlementaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a boy at a school desk placing tiny wooden figures into the rows of little red seats of a half-circle model of a parliament chamber. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 into this room.
fr_parlementaire_adj.note: Cognate of English parliamentary. Parlementaire means parliamentary (un régime parlementaire; le débat parlementaire). As a noun, un or une parlementaire is a member of parliament. Its root is parler, to speak. Do not confuse it with parlementer, to negotiate.

fr_autoritaire_adj.hook: "oh-toh-ree-TEHR": a strict gray-haired schoolmistress frowns and raises her ruler, about to rap the desk: AUTHORITARIAN: AUTHORITARIAN
fr_autoritaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a strict older schoolmistress with a tight gray bun and a high collar, frowning and raising a wooden ruler to rap it on her desk.
fr_autoritaire_adj.note: Cognate of English authoritarian. Autoritaire means authoritarian or bossy (un régime autoritaire; un père autoritaire). It is a criticism, stronger than strict (sévère). Its opposite is libéral, permissif or souple. L'autorité is authority.

fr_theoriquement_adv.hook: "tay-oh-ree-kuh-MAHN": two children kneel by their real paper plane, crashed on the floor, right under the perfect chalk flight path on the board: it works THEORETICALLY: THEORETICALLY
fr_theoriquement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): two children kneeling on the floor under the chalkboard beside their real paper plane, which lies crashed on the floor, below a perfect curving dotted chalk flight path ending in a chalk paper plane. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_theoriquement_adv.note: Cognate of English theoretically. Théoriquement means theoretically or in principle, and it often hints that reality will differ (Théoriquement, il arrive à 8 h = He's supposed to arrive at 8). Its opposite is pratiquement or en pratique. Une théorie is a theory.

fr_fondamentalement_adv.hook: "fohn-dah-mahn-tah-luh-MAHN": a girl points at the big bottom block that holds up her whole tall tower: FUNDAMENTALLY: FUNDAMENTALLY
fr_fondamentalement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a girl sitting on the floor pointing at the big wide base block at the bottom of her tall tower of wooden blocks. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_04 into this room.
fr_fondamentalement_adv.note: Cognate of English fundamentally. Fondamentalement means fundamentally, at its very base (Ils sont fondamentalement différents). It comes from fondamental and le fondement, the foundation. Its opposite is superficiellement, superficially.

fr_socialisme_noun.hook: "soh-syah-LEEZM": three workers in overalls share out the round loaves on one table equally: SOCIALISM: SOCIALISM
fr_socialisme_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): three workers in blue overalls and red neckerchiefs standing together at one table, sharing out two big round loaves of bread. Moved from the planned room R_society_03 into this room.
fr_socialisme_noun.note: Cognate of English socialism. Le socialisme is socialism, the political idea of sharing wealth and owning key industries together (le socialisme utopique; le Parti socialiste). Its opposite is le capitalisme or le libéralisme. A follower is un or une socialiste.

fr_gouvernant_noun.hook: "goo-vehr-NAHN": a boy dressed as a king in a paper crown sits on a big carved chair, GOVERNING the class: a RULER: GOVERNING
fr_gouvernant_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/institutions (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a small boy about eight years old dressed as a king in a gold paper crown and a red cape, sitting on a big carved wooden chair and holding a toy scepter. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_gouvernant_noun.note: Cognate of English governing (from gouverner, to govern). Un gouvernant is a ruler; it is mostly used in the plural, les gouvernants, those in power, as opposed to les gouvernés, the governed. Careful: une gouvernante is a housekeeper or governess, not a female ruler.

fr_inauguration_noun.hook: "ee-noh-gew-rah-SYOHN": the mayor in her blue-white-red sash snips the ribbon to open the new wing: the INAUGURATION: INAUGURATION
fr_inauguration_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a woman mayor wearing a blue-white-red sash across her chest, cutting a wide blue-white-red ribbon stretched between two brass stands with a pair of ordinary gold scissors.
fr_inauguration_noun.note: Cognate of English inauguration. Une inauguration is the official opening of a new building, road or exhibition (l'inauguration de la nouvelle école), usually with a ribbon cut by the mayor. It can also mean the start of a term of office, but that sense is rarer in French than in English. The verb is inaugurer.

fr_presidence_noun.hook: "pray-zee-DAHNS": a woman rings the little brass bell from the tall gilded presiding chair: she holds the PRESIDENCY of the evening: PRESIDENCY
fr_presidence_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a woman in a dark blue dress seated in a tall gilded armchair with a red velvet seat, ringing a little brass hand bell.
fr_presidence_noun.note: Cognate of English presidency. La présidence is the presidency, the office of president or its term (pendant sa présidence), and also the chairing of a meeting or body (assurer la présidence de la séance). La présidence also names the president's offices and staff (un communiqué de la présidence).

fr_accession_noun.hook: "ahk-seh-SYOHN": a little girl in a yellow dress climbs the last red-carpeted step up onto the stage: her ACCESSION to the top: ACCESSION
fr_accession_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a little girl in a yellow dress climbing, one foot raised, the last of three red-carpeted steps up onto the low wooden stage beside the tall presiding chair. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_accession_noun.note: Cognate of English accession. L'accession is reaching a rank or a status (l'accession au trône; l'accession à l'indépendance). L'accession à la propriété means becoming a homeowner. It is a formal word; in everyday French people say l'accès or say arriver à.

fr_nomination_noun.hook: "noh-mee-nah-SYOHN": a man reads a name off his card and a young woman jumps up, hand on her heart: her NOMINATION: NOMINATION
fr_nomination_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a man in a dark suit reading from a small card, and beside him a young woman standing up from a gilded chair with one hand on her heart in delighted surprise. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 into this room.
fr_nomination_noun.note: Cognate of English nomination. Une nomination is usually an appointment to a post (sa nomination au poste de directeur), not only a proposal. It is also a nomination for a prize (trois nominations aux César). The verb is nommer, to appoint or to name.

fr_institutionnel_adj.hook: "ans-tee-tew-syoh-NEHL": on a stand stands the white model of the grand domed public building, the new INSTITUTION being opened: INSTITUTIONAL
fr_institutionnel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a white model of a grand public building with columns and a dome, standing on a wooden stand. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_institutionnel_adj.note: Cognate of English institutional. Institutionnel means about institutions, the official bodies of the state (la réforme institutionnelle; une crise institutionnelle). Fem. institutionnelle. Une institution is an institution; une institutrice, un instituteur was the old word for a primary school teacher. Its opposite is informel.

fr_republicain_adj.hook: "ray-pew-blee-KAN": a white bust of Marianne in her soft cap, the symbol of the French Republic, stands on a pedestal: REPUBLICAN: REPUBLICAN
fr_republicain_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a white plaster bust of Marianne, a young woman with long hair wearing a soft floppy Phrygian cap that folds forward (not a helmet), on a tall white pedestal against the back wall. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_republicain_adj.note: Cognate of English republican. Républicain means of the Republic or loyal to it (les valeurs républicaines; la garde républicaine). In France it is not a party label as in the US; Les Républicains is the name of one right-wing party. Its opposite is monarchiste or royaliste.

fr_resolument_adv.hook: "ray-zoh-lew-MAHN": a little drummer boy marches across the hall, jaw set and eyes straight ahead: RESOLUTELY: RESOLUTELY
fr_resolument_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a little boy in a red jacket with a drum on a strap, marching with a determined set jaw, eyes straight ahead, drumsticks raised. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_04 into this room.
fr_resolument_adv.note: Cognate of English resolutely. Résolument means resolutely, with firm determination (Elle est résolument contre ce projet). It often means decidedly or firmly in a style (un hôtel résolument moderne). It comes from résolu, determined. Its opposite is timidement or mollement.

fr_grandiose_adj.hook: "grahn-DYOHZ": an enormous five-tier white wedding-style cake stands right on the parquet floor in the middle of the hall: GRANDIOSE: GRANDIOSE
fr_grandiose_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an enormous white cake with five stacked tiers, each smaller than the one below, standing straight on the parquet floor on a round silver board. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_06 into this room.
fr_grandiose_adj.note: Cognate of English grandiose. Grandiose means magnificent or grand, and in French it is usually praise (un paysage grandiose; une cérémonie grandiose). In English grandiose often sounds pompous. Its opposite is modeste or mesquin.

fr_prestigieux_adj.hook: "prehs-tee-ZHYEUH": a famous old actress in a white fur stole proudly holds up a glossy portrait of herself for her fans: a PRESTIGIOUS guest: PRESTIGIOUS
fr_prestigieux_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): an elegant elderly white-haired actress in a white gown and a white fur stole, standing just behind the cake, holding up a big glossy portrait photograph of her own face in both hands. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_05 into this room.
fr_prestigieux_adj.note: Cognate of English prestigious. Prestigieux means prestigious, admired and famous (une école prestigieuse; un prix prestigieux). Fem. prestigieuse. Le prestige is prestige. In older French it meant an illusion or a magic trick, a sense that is now lost.

fr_formellement_adv.hook: "for-meh-luh-MAHN": a butler in tails and white gloves bows stiffly, very FORMALLY, holding out a silver tray: FORMALLY
fr_formellement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a butler in a black tailcoat and white gloves bowing stiffly and formally while holding out a silver tray of glasses. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_04 into this room.
fr_formellement_adv.note: Cognate of English formally. Formellement means formally, according to the rules (Il a été formellement invité), but very often it means strictly or explicitly (C'est formellement interdit = It is strictly forbidden; Je le nie formellement = I flatly deny it). Its opposite is vaguement or officieusement.

fr_vice_president_noun.hook: "vees-pray-zee-DAHN": a man sits in a second gilded chair, a little smaller than the presiding one: the VICE-PRESIDENT: VICE-PRESIDENT
fr_vice_president_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a man in a gray suit seated in a small gilded armchair with a red velvet seat, a smaller copy of the tall presiding chair, hands on his knees. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 into this room.
fr_vice_president_noun.note: Cognate of English vice-president. Un vice-président, une vice-présidente is a vice-president, the deputy of a president or chair (le vice-président du conseil départemental). France has no vice-president of the Republic: if the president leaves office, the president of the Senate stands in.

fr_senateur_noun.hook: "say-nah-TUHR": a dignified white-haired SENATOR in a dark suit listens with his hands folded on his cane: SENATOR
fr_senateur_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/inauguration (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE4 build): a dignified white-haired old man in a dark three-piece suit with a pocket watch chain, standing and listening with both hands folded on top of a walking cane. Moved from the planned room R_politics_02 into this room.
fr_senateur_noun.note: Cognate of English senator. Un sénateur, une sénatrice is a senator, a member of the Sénat, France's upper house of parliament, elected indirectly by local councilors (le sénateur de la Corrèze). Its partner is le député, who sits in the Assemblée nationale.

fr_collectivite_noun.hook: "koh-lehk-tee-vee-TAY": a grandmother, a father carrying a toddler and a teenage girl stand together arm in arm: the local COMMUNITY, la collectivité: COLLECTIVITY
fr_collectivite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a grandmother, a father carrying a toddler on his arm and a teenage girl standing close together, arms around each other's shoulders. Moved from the planned room R_society_03 into this room.
fr_collectivite_noun.note: Cognate of English collectivity. Une collectivité is a community, a group of people living together (la vie en collectivité = communal living), and above all a local authority: une collectivité territoriale (or locale) is a commune, a département or a région, which runs local services. It is not a collection of objects: that is une collection.

fr_concession_noun.hook: "kohn-say-SYOHN": a man raises his palms and gives way, letting a woman plant her toy tree on the model: a CONCESSION
fr_concession_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a man raising both open palms and stepping back to give way to a woman in a red cardigan who plants a little toy tree on a small model table. Moved from the planned room R_society_02 into this room.
fr_concession_noun.note: Cognate of English concession. Une concession is something you give up in a deal (faire des concessions = to compromise), and also a right granted by the state to use land or run a service (une concession d'autoroute), a burial plot in a cemetery, and a car dealership (un concessionnaire runs one). Sans concession means uncompromising.
