fr_rural_adj.hook: "rew-RAHL": a girl kneels beside a toy farm with a red barn, haystacks and cows in green fields: RURAL
fr_rural_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a girl kneeling on the floor beside a toy farm on a square of green felt: a red barn, two haystacks and little cows. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_rural_adj.note: Cognate of English rural. Rural means of the countryside (une commune rurale; l'exode rural = the drift from the land; le monde rural). It is the same in the masculine and feminine; plural ruraux. Its opposite is urbain.

fr_urbain_adj.hook: "ewr-BAN": a boy carries a model of tall gray tower blocks and busy little streets: URBAN
fr_urbain_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a teenage boy carrying in both arms a big model of gray tower blocks with tiny busy streets between them.
fr_urbain_adj.note: Cognate of English urban. Urbain means of the town or city (les transports urbains; le paysage urbain; un chauffage urbain = district heating). In formal French it also means urbane, polite and refined, though that sense is now rare. Fem. urbaine. Its opposite is rural.

fr_isole_adj.hook: "ee-zoh-LAY": a single tiny model house sits alone on a little island in a glass bowl of water: ISOLATED
fr_isole_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a big glass bowl of water on a low stool, with one tiny model house alone on a little island in the middle of the water. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_isole_adj.note: Cognate of English isolated. Isolé means isolated or remote (un hameau isolé; se sentir isolé = to feel lonely) and also single or one-off (un cas isolé). Fem. isolée. For a building it also means insulated (une maison bien isolée). Its opposite is entouré or, for a place, central.

fr_renouvelable_adj.hook: "ruh-noo-vuh-LAHBL": a white model wind turbine stands by a small solar panel catching the sun: RENEWABLE energy
fr_renouvelable_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): standing on the floor by the back wall, a child-high white model wind turbine with three blades, a small solar panel leaning at its foot. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_09 into this room.
fr_renouvelable_adj.note: Cognate of English renewable. Renouvelable means renewable (les énergies renouvelables = renewable energy) and also, of a contract or a permit, able to be renewed (un contrat d'un an renouvelable). Its opposite is non renouvelable. The verb is renouveler.

fr_ecologique_adj.hook: "ay-koh-loh-ZHEEK": a green bicycle on its kickstand with a basket of vegetables, the ECOLOGICAL way to get to the town hall
fr_ecologique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a green bicycle on its kickstand with a wicker basket full of fresh vegetables.
fr_ecologique_adj.note: Cognate of English ecological. Écologique means ecological, about the environment (une catastrophe écologique), and very often eco-friendly or green (un produit écologique; un geste écologique). Un ou une écologiste is an environmentalist; in politics people say les Verts. Its opposite is polluant.

fr_municipal_adj.hook: "mew-nee-see-PAHL": the town cleaner in his orange vest sweeps the floor with a green broom: a MUNICIPAL worker
fr_municipal_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): the town cleaner in an orange vest and green work trousers sweeping the floor with a long green broom. Moved from the planned room R_politics_02 into this room.
fr_municipal_adj.note: Cognate of English municipal. Municipal means of the town or its council (le conseil municipal = the town council; la piscine municipale; les élections municipales). Fem. municipale; plural municipaux. La municipalité is the town council. Its opposite is privé or, for a wider area, national.

fr_progressif_adj.hook: "proh-gray-SEEF": four potted trees in a row by the window, each taller than the last: PROGRESSIVE growth
fr_progressif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): by the back window, four potted trees in a row, each one taller than the last. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_progressif_adj.note: Cognate of English progressive. Progressif mostly means gradual, step by step (une baisse progressive; des lunettes progressives = varifocals). In politics, progressiste is the usual word for progressive. Fem. progressive. Its opposite is brusque or soudain.

fr_central_adj.hook: "sahn-TRAHL": a planner pushes a big red pin into the exact center of the round village model: CENTRAL
fr_central_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a planner in a gray suit pushing a big red pin into the exact center of a round village model on a small round table. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_05 into this room.
fr_central_adj.note: Cognate of English central. Central means central, in the middle or the most important (le quartier central; le rôle central; le chauffage central = central heating). La centrale is a power station (une centrale nucléaire). Plural centraux. Its opposite is périphérique or isolé.

fr_departemental_adj.hook: "day-pahr-tuh-mahn-TAHL": a big wooden jigsaw map of France stands on an easel, each piece one département: DEPARTMENTAL
fr_departemental_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a big wooden jigsaw map of France on an easel, made of many small pieces in different soft colors, one piece lifted out on the easel ledge. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_02 into this room.
fr_departemental_adj.note: Cognate of English departmental. Départemental means of a French département, one of the 101 areas between the commune and the région (une route départementale = a secondary road; le conseil départemental). Fem. départementale. In a company or shop, de service or du rayon is the usual way to say departmental.

fr_accessible_adj.hook: "ahk-say-SEEBL": a young man in a wheelchair rolls easily up the new gentle wooden ramp: ACCESSIBLE
fr_accessible_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a young man in a blue hoodie in a wheelchair rolling easily up a short gentle wooden ramp. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_09 into this room.
fr_accessible_adj.note: Cognate of English accessible. Accessible means easy to reach or enter (un bâtiment accessible aux fauteuils roulants), easy to understand (un livre accessible), and also affordable (des prix accessibles). Its opposite is inaccessible. A person who is open and approachable is also accessible.

fr_resident_noun.hook: "ray-zee-DAHN": a man in slippers and a cardigan proudly holds up the model of his own house with his door keys: a RESIDENT
fr_resident_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/environnement (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a man in slippers and a dark cardigan proudly holding up a little model of his own house in one hand and a ring of door keys in the other. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_resident_noun.note: Cognate of English resident. Un résident, une résidente is a resident, someone who lives in a place, often a foreigner living in a country (les résidents étrangers) or someone living in a care home (une résidence). A local living in a town is more often un habitant. Une résidence secondaire is a second home.

fr_transaction_noun.hook: "trahn-zahk-SYOHN": at the counter a woman hands over green banknotes and the clerk hands her a rolled deed: a TRANSACTION
fr_transaction_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a woman in a green coat at a short wooden counter handing a bundle of plain green banknotes to a clerk in a gray waistcoat who hands her a rolled paper deed tied with a ribbon. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 into this room.
fr_transaction_noun.note: Cognate of English transaction. Une transaction is a deal or a payment (une transaction bancaire; une transaction immobilière = a property sale). In law it is also a settlement, a compromise reached to end a dispute (trouver une transaction), and in old or formal French a concession. Its opposite in that sense is un procès (a lawsuit).

fr_capitaliste_adj.hook: "kah-pih-tah-LEEST": a businessman in a top hat and a striped suit stacks tall towers of gold coins on his desk: CAPITALIST
fr_capitaliste_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a portly businessman in a top hat and a pinstriped suit sitting at a small desk, stacking plain gold coins into several tall towers.
fr_capitaliste_adj.note: Cognate of English capitalist. Capitaliste means capitalist (l'économie capitaliste; un pays capitaliste). Un or une capitaliste is a capitalist, an owner of capital. Its opposite is socialiste or communiste. Le capital is capital; la capitale is a capital city.

fr_foncier_adj.hook: "fohn-SYAY": a farmer on an old telephone cheers: "YAY!" PHONE-SEE-YAY: his field is sold, and the land deed lies by his knee (foncier = land): PHONE-YAY
fr_foncier_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a farmer in a straw hat and blue overalls kneeling on the carpet, cheering into an old black telephone, a paper land deed on the floor by his knee. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_08 into this room.
fr_foncier_adj.note: Foncier means about land and property: un terrain, un bien foncier (land, real estate), l'impôt foncier or la taxe foncière (property tax), un propriétaire foncier (a landowner). In a second sense it means basic or deep, part of someone's nature (une qualité foncière; il est foncièrement honnête = he is honest to the core). Its opposite in that sense is superficiel.

fr_lucratif_adj.hook: "lew-krah-TEEF": a girl's tin cash box overflows with banknotes and coins from her lemonade stand: LUCRATIVE
fr_lucratif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a girl with pigtails behind a little wooden lemonade stand with a glass jug of lemonade, her open tin cash box overflowing with plain green banknotes and gold coins.
fr_lucratif_adj.note: Cognate of English lucrative. Lucratif means profitable, bringing in money (un métier lucratif; une affaire lucrative). Fem. lucrative. Une association à but non lucratif is a non-profit organization. Its opposite is déficitaire or peu rentable.

fr_exorbitant_adj.hook: "ehg-zor-bee-TAHN": a shocked man pays for one small teacup with a whole wheelbarrow heaped with banknotes: EXORBITANT
fr_exorbitant_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a man in a tweed cap with his mouth wide open in shock, pushing a wooden wheelbarrow heaped with plain green banknotes, holding up one small white teacup in his other hand.
fr_exorbitant_adj.note: Cognate of English exorbitant. Exorbitant means far too high, outrageous (un prix exorbitant; des loyers exorbitants). Fem. exorbitante. It is used of prices, demands and privileges. Its opposite is raisonnable or modique (modest).

fr_couteux_adj.hook: "koo-TEUH": a black COOT bird wears a sparkling diamond necklace on a velvet cushion: KOO-TEUH, so costly
fr_couteux_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a black coot bird with a white beak sitting on a red velvet cushion on a low wooden stand, wearing a sparkling diamond necklace. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_06 into this room.
fr_couteux_adj.note: Coûteux means costly, expensive (un voyage coûteux; une erreur coûteuse = a costly mistake). Fem. coûteuse. It comes from coûter, to cost. In everyday speech cher is more common. Its opposite is bon marché or économique (cheap, economical).

fr_inestimable_adj.hook: "ee-nehs-tee-MAHBL": a jeweled golden crown sits in a glass case beside the safe, worth more than any price: INESTIMABLE: INESTIMABLE, priceless
fr_inestimable_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a jeweled golden crown on a red cushion inside a glass display case on a slim pedestal.
fr_inestimable_adj.note: Cognate of English inestimable. Inestimable means priceless, too valuable to put a price on (un tableau d'une valeur inestimable), and of help or advice, invaluable (une aide inestimable). It is never negative. Its opposite is sans valeur (worthless).

fr_enrichissant_adj.hook: "ahn-ree-shee-SAHN": a grandfather shows a girl a tray of old coins and tells her their stories; she learns a lot: ENRICHING
fr_enrichissant_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a white-haired grandfather showing a girl a tray of old coins at a small table as she listens, fascinated.
fr_enrichissant_adj.note: Cognate of English enriching. Enrichissant means enriching, rewarding because you learn or grow (une expérience enrichissante; un échange enrichissant). It is the present participle of enrichir (to make rich), but it is about the mind, not money. Its opposite is ennuyeux or stérile.

fr_global_adj.hook: "gloh-BAHL": a woman spins a big globe on a wooden stand: GLOBAL
fr_global_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a woman in a mustard cardigan spinning a big globe on a wooden floor stand, with blue seas and green land and no writing. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_06 into this room.
fr_global_adj.note: Cognate of English global. Global means worldwide (le réchauffement global), but very often it means total or overall, taken as a whole (le coût global; une vision globale; une somme globale). Its opposite in that sense is partiel or détaillé.

fr_pleinement_adv.hook: "pleh-nuh-MAHN": a jolly round PLENTY-MAN fills a big glass jar with candies right up to the very brim: fully, PLEINEMENT
fr_pleinement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a jolly round man with rosy cheeks pouring colorful wrapped candies from a paper bag into a big glass jar that is filled right up to the brim. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_pleinement_adv.note: Pleinement means fully, completely (Je suis pleinement satisfait; vivre pleinement = to live life to the full). It comes from plein, full. It is formal; in speech people often say complètement or tout à fait. Its opposite is partiellement (partly) or à moitié (half).

fr_externe_adj.hook: "ehk-STEHRN": a window cleaner on a ladder OUTSIDE the tall window squeegees the glass: he works on the EXTERNAL side
fr_externe_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): outdoors, beyond the closed glass of the tall back window: a window cleaner in blue overalls on a ladder leaning on the outside wall, wiping the outer side of the glass with a squeegee.
fr_externe_adj.note: Cognate of English external. Externe means external, outside (un auditeur externe; à usage externe = for external use only, on medicine). Its opposite is interne. Un externe at school is a day pupil who goes home for lunch, and in a hospital a medical student.

fr_strategique_adj.hook: "strah-tay-ZHEEK": a man and a woman lean over a checkerboard, planning their next move: STRATEGIC
fr_strategique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a man and a woman at a small square table leaning over a checkerboard, planning their next move. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_06 into this room.
fr_strategique_adj.note: Cognate of English strategic. Stratégique means strategic, about long-term planning or military strategy (un plan stratégique; un point stratégique = a key position). It can also mean tactical, calculated (une retraite stratégique). Its opposite is improvisé or, for a place, secondaire.

fr_consultatif_adj.hook: "kohn-sewl-tah-TEEF": an adviser whispers into the treasurer's ear; the treasurer listens but decides: CONSULTATIVE
fr_consultatif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a slim adviser in a gray suit bending to whisper into the ear of a seated treasurer in a waistcoat who listens with his hand on an open ledger. Moved from the planned room R_politics_04 into this room.
fr_consultatif_adj.note: Cognate of English consultative. Consultatif means advisory: it may give advice but cannot decide (un comité consultatif; avoir une voix consultative = to have a say but no vote). Fem. consultative. Its opposite is délibératif or décisionnel (with power to decide).

fr_mandataire_noun.hook: "mahn-dah-TEHR": a young man signs the big ledger in his grandmother's name while she hands him her signed letter and pen: her MANDATARY: MANDATARY, proxy
fr_mandataire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/budget (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): an elderly lady with a cane handing a signed letter and a fountain pen to her grandson, a young man in a blue sweater who leans over a big open ledger on a tall wooden desk to sign it for her. Moved from the planned room R_admin_02 into this room.
fr_mandataire_noun.note: Cognate of English mandatary. Un or une mandataire is a proxy or agent, someone authorized to act in another person's name (le mandataire d'un client; voter par mandataire). In business, un mandataire immobilier is an independent real estate agent, and un mandataire judiciaire is a court-appointed administrator. The person who gives the authority is le mandant.

fr_precarite_noun.hook: "pray-kah-ree-TAY": a woman in a worn coat counts the last few coins in her open purse, her shopping bag nearly empty: PRECARITY
fr_precarite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a tired woman in a worn brown coat sitting on a bench, counting three small coins in her palm over an open purse, a nearly empty shopping bag at her feet. Moved from the planned room R_society_04 into this room.
fr_precarite_noun.note: Cognate of English precarity. La précarité is insecurity, living without a stable job, home or income (la précarité de l'emploi; vivre dans la précarité). It also means fragility, of anything that may not last (la précarité de la paix). The adjective is précaire. Its opposite is la stabilité or la sécurité.

fr_revendication_noun.hook: "ruh-vahn-dee-kah-SYOHN": a woman firmly points at her red toy VAN on the lost-and-found shelf and claims it back: ruh-VAHN-dee… her claim, her demand: VAN-DEMAND
fr_revendication_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a determined woman in a purple coat standing at a lost-and-found shelf, pointing firmly at a small red toy van on it with one hand, her other hand on her hip.
fr_revendication_noun.note: Une revendication is a claim or a demand, something people insist is theirs by right (les revendications des salariés; une revendication territoriale). It also means claiming responsibility for an act (la revendication d'un attentat). The verb is revendiquer. Its opposite is la renonciation (giving up a claim).

fr_utopie_noun.hook: "ew-toh-PEA": a girl at an easel paints a perfect dream town of rainbows, gardens and smiling houses: UTOPIA
fr_utopie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a girl at an easel painting a bright dream town with rainbows, flower gardens and round smiling houses on her canvas.
fr_utopie_noun.note: Cognate of English utopia. Une utopie is a utopia, an ideal society (L'Utopie of Thomas More), and very often an impossible dream (C'est une utopie = It will never happen). The adjective is utopique. Its opposite is le réalisme or, for a society, une dystopie.

fr_petition_noun.hook: "pay-tee-SYOHN": a woman holds out a clipboard with a long blank PETITION, and a man adds his signature
fr_petition_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a woman holding out a clipboard with a long blank sheet of paper while a man in a flat cap signs it with a pen. Moved from the planned room R_politics_05 into this room.
fr_petition_noun.note: Cognate of English petition. Une pétition is a petition signed by many people (signer une pétition; lancer une pétition en ligne). In logic, une pétition de principe is begging the question, assuming what you want to prove. Its opposite, a counter-petition, is une contre-pétition.

fr_reinsertion_noun.hook: "ray-an-sehr-SYOHN": a cook shakes hands with a young woman tying on her new apron: welcome back into the team, her REINSERTION: REINSERTION, back in
fr_reinsertion_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a smiling cook in a white jacket shaking hands with a young woman who is tying on a new green apron, welcoming her to the kitchen team.
fr_reinsertion_noun.note: Cognate of English reinsertion. La réinsertion is reintegration, helping someone back into society or work after prison, illness or long unemployment (la réinsertion professionnelle; la réinsertion sociale). It can also mean putting a part back in. Its opposite is l'exclusion.

fr_collectif_adj.hook: "koh-lehk-TEEF": three children carry one long table together, one at each end and one in the middle: a COLLECTIVE effort
fr_collectif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): three children, two boys and a girl, carrying one long folding table together across the hall, one at each end and one in the middle. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_collectif_adj.note: Cognate of English collective. Collectif means collective, done or shared by a group (un effort collectif; un sport collectif = a team sport; les transports collectifs = public transport). Fem. collective. Un collectif is a group or collective. Its opposite is individuel.

fr_humanitaire_adj.hook: "ew-mah-nee-TEHR": a volunteer in a blue vest stacks boxes of food and blankets for families in need: HUMANITARIAN aid
fr_humanitaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a volunteer in a plain blue vest stacking plain cardboard boxes of food and folded gray blankets onto a hand trolley. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_03 into this room.
fr_humanitaire_adj.note: Cognate of English humanitarian. Humanitaire means humanitarian (l'aide humanitaire; une crise humanitaire; une organisation humanitaire). Un or une humanitaire is an aid worker, and l'humanitaire is aid work as a field (travailler dans l'humanitaire). Its opposite is inhumain.

fr_eventuellement_adv.hook: "ay-vahn-tweh-luh-MAHN": a boy packs for every EVENTUALITY: a raincoat in one hand and swimming goggles in the other, because possibly it will rain, possibly they'll swim
fr_eventuellement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a boy in shorts standing by an open backpack, holding up a yellow raincoat in one hand and blue swimming goggles in the other, looking up thoughtfully. Moved from the planned room R_adv_logic_05 into this room.
fr_eventuellement_adv.note: False friend: NOT 'eventually'. Éventuellement means possibly, if need be (Je viendrai éventuellement = I may come; Vous pouvez éventuellement payer par carte = You can pay by card if you like). Eventually is finalement or à la longue. The adjective éventuel means possible (un éventuel retard), and une éventualité is a possibility. Its opposite is certainement.

fr_communautaire_adj.hook: "koh-mew-noh-TEHR": a cook ladles soup from the huge shared COMMUNAL pot into bowls for everyone: COMMUNITY, communal
fr_communautaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a cook in a white apron ladling soup from a huge steaming pot on a trestle table into a row of white bowls.
fr_communautaire_adj.note: Cognate of English communitarian. Communautaire means of a community (la vie communautaire; un jardin communautaire = a community garden) and, in politics, of the European Union (le droit communautaire). Le communautarisme is putting your own group first. Its opposite is individuel or, for the EU, national.

fr_domestique_adj.hook: "doh-mehs-TEEK": a man irons a shirt on an ironing board, a DOMESTIC chore
fr_domestique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a man in a checked shirt pressing a white shirt with an iron on an ironing board, a neat stack of folded laundry beside him. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_domestique_adj.note: Cognate of English domestic. Domestique means of the home (les tâches domestiques = household chores; un animal domestique = a pet; un accident domestique). It also means within a country (le marché domestique; un vol domestique is more often un vol intérieur). Un or une domestique is a servant. Its opposite is sauvage (for animals) or international.

fr_natal_adj.hook: "nah-TAHL": an old man hugs a painting of the little village where he was born: his NATIVE village: NATAL, native
fr_natal_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a white-haired old man in a flat cap hugging a framed painting of a little hilltop village with a church tower to his chest, eyes closed, smiling. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_04 into this room.
fr_natal_adj.note: Cognate of English natal. Natal means native, where you were born (mon village natal; sa langue natale = mother tongue, more often langue maternelle). Plural natals. It is not about birth itself, which is la naissance; prénatal and postnatal are about pregnancy. Its opposite is d'adoption (un pays d'adoption).

fr_representatif_adj.hook: "ruh-pray-zahn-tah-TEEF": a delegate stands at a small lectern to speak for all the volunteers: REPRESENTATIVE
fr_representatif_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a woman delegate in a navy blazer standing at a small wooden lectern, speaking with one open hand raised toward the room. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_representatif_adj.note: Cognate of English representative. Représentatif means representative: typical of a group (un échantillon représentatif = a representative sample) or acting for others (la démocratie représentative). Fem. représentative. A representative person is un représentant. Its opposite is atypique or peu représentatif.

fr_solidaire_adj.hook: "soh-lee-DEHR": even on crutches, a boy carries a shopping bag for the soup kitchen: everyone stands together, SOLIDAIRE: SOLIDARY, standing together
fr_solidaire_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a boy on crutches carrying a shopping bag of groceries for the soup kitchen. Moved from the planned room R_adj_relation_10 into this room.
fr_solidaire_adj.note: Cognate of English solidary. Solidaire means showing solidarity, supporting each other (être solidaire de ses collègues; une économie solidaire). It also means bound together, dependent on each other (des pièces solidaires = linked parts). La solidarité is solidarity. Its opposite is égoïste or indifférent.

fr_manifestant_noun.hook: "mah-nee-fehs-TAHN": a marcher holds up a blank placard, and a big toy ANT rides on his shoulder: MANIFEST-ANT, a protester
fr_manifestant_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): a young man in a striped scarf marching on the spot with a blank white placard on a stick raised high, a big red toy ant sitting on his shoulder.
fr_manifestant_noun.note: Un manifestant, une manifestante is a protester, someone taking part in a demonstration (une manifestation, une manif). The verb is manifester, which also means to show (manifester sa joie). It does not mean a manifest or a passenger list. Its opposite is un contre-manifestant (counter-protester) or un spectateur.

fr_us_noun.hook: "EWS": two woolly EWES curtsy to each other very politely: the old customs and manners, les us et coutumes
fr_us_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/solidarite (Nov 1 2026 MAIRIE6 build): two woolly white sheep standing on their hind legs, curtsying politely to each other with one front leg bent.
fr_us_noun.note: Les us (always plural, pronounced with the s) are customs and manners, only in the set phrase les us et coutumes (the ways and customs of a place). It is old-fashioned and formal. Don't mix it up with US (les États-Unis). Its opposite is la nouveauté or les mœurs modernes.
